AMERICA, THE MIDTERM ELECTIONS MATTER MORE THAN YOU THINK!
My family is deeply concerned about our country's direction and the growing influence of political movements that challenge the principles on which America was founded.  We are witnessing increasingly heated debates over socialism, communism, religious extremism, individual liberty, and the proper role of government.  These are not insignificant disagreements.  They concern the very future of our constitutional republic.
Our universities have become battlegrounds for competing ideologies, and young Americans are being offered promises of government-funded benefits without an equally serious discussion of their costs, consequences, or limits.  Young people deserve an education that teaches them to question political promises, examine evidence, understand history, and think independently rather than simply embrace whatever ideology happens to be fashionable.
I believe in religious freedom, but I also believe that our Constitution must remain the foundation of American government.  No religious or political ideology should supersede the rights and liberties guaranteed to every American.  Freedom of speech, freedom of worship, individual responsibility, and equal protection under the law are principles worth defending, regardless of which political party holds power.
THE MIDTERM ELECTIONS ARE NOT SOMETHING WE CAN AFFORD TO IGNORE!
Every eligible American should understand what is at stake, examine the candidates and their records, and participate in the democratic process.  Do not assume someone else will cast the vote that you choose not to cast.  Do not allow frustration, complacency, or political fatigue to silence your voice.
Our parents, grandparents, and generations before us made tremendous sacrifices to preserve the freedoms we enjoy today.  The least we can do is take those freedoms seriously enough to participate in deciding how our country is governed.
AMERICA’S FUTURE IS NOT SOMEONE ELSE’S RESPONSIBILITY.  IT BELONGS TO ALL OF US.
Get informed.  Talk with your family.  Help eligible voters understand how to participate.  And above all, exercise the precious right that so many Americans sacrificed to protect.

text:
In city where the pagans murdered a Christian Bishop. Julian the Apostate writes:

In the tenth month, according to your reckoning, - Loos I think you call it - there is a festival founded by your forefathers in honour of this god, and it was your duty to be zealous in visiting Daphne. Accordingly I hastened thither from the temple and f Zeus’s. thinking that at Daphne, if anywhere, I should enjoy the sight of your wealth and public spirit. 

And I imagined in my own mind the sort of procession it would be, like a man seeing visions in a dream. beasts for sacrifice, libations, choruses in honour of the god, incense, and the youths of your city there surrounding the shrine, their souls adorned with all holiness and themselves attired in white and splendid raiment. 

But when I entered the shrine I found there no incense, not so much as a cake, not a single beast for sacrifice. For that moment I was amazed and thought that I was still outside the shrine and that you were waiting the signal from me, ￼doing me that honour because I am supreme pontiff. But when I began to inquire what sacrifice the city intended to offer to celebrate the annual festival in honour of the god, the priest answered, "I have brought with me from my own house a goose as an offering to the god, but the city at this time made no preparations. 

Thereupon, being fond of making enemies, I made in the Senate a very unseemly speech which perhaps it may now be pertinent to quote to you. "It is a terrible thing," I said, "that so important a city should be more neglectful of the gods than any village on the borders of the Pontus.

text:
Here’s my take @grok what are your AI outputs on my inputs? The four quadrants of the gospels are key.

The Fig Tree: A Four-Dimensional Lesson in Fruitlessness

The fig tree incident is one of the most misunderstood passages in the Gospels. Critics say it makes Jesus look petty—cursing a tree for not having fruit out of season. But read through the four Gospel lenses, it becomes a devastating prophetic act about fruitlessness and judgment.

Matthew 21:18-22 (King Quadrant). Matthew presents Jesus as the King with authority. He curses the fig tree, and it withers immediately. The disciples are amazed, and Jesus uses it as a lesson on faith: "If you have faith and do not doubt... even the mountains will move." Here, the King demonstrates authority over creation and teaches that trust in YHWH produces power. The fruitless tree represents Israel—full of leaves (religious appearance) but no fruit (obedience). The King pronounces judgment.

Mark 11:12-14, 20-25 (Servant Quadrant). Mark sandwiches the fig tree around the temple cleansing. Jesus curses the tree on the way to Jerusalem, then cleanses the temple, then the next day the tree is withered. Mark's emphasis is on immediate action and the corruption of the temple system. The fig tree symbolizes the temple: it looks alive (leafy) but produces nothing. The Servant-King judges fruitlessness. Mark also ties it to prayer and forgiveness—trust in YHWH, not religious performance.

Luke (Man Quadrant). Luke doesn't record the fig tree. Instead, he gives us the parable of the barren fig tree (Luke 13:6-9), where the gardener pleads for one more year. Luke's focus is compassion and repentance. The tree is given time to bear fruit. But if it still doesn't, it will be cut down. The Man quadrant emphasizes YHWH's patience—but also the certainty of judgment if fruitlessness persists.

John (Eagle Quadrant). John doesn't include the fig tree either. But his Gospel is full of fruit-bearing language: "I am the vine; you are the branches. Whoever abides in me and I in him, he it is that bears much fruit" (John 15:5). The Eagle perspective sees the eternal reality: fruit is the evidence of abiding in Christ. Without it, you are cut off.

The "Out of Season" Objection. The text says it wasn't the season for figs (Mark 11:13). But the tree had leaves—and in fig trees, leaves normally indicate fruit. Jesus found only leaves, a picture of hypocrisy: the appearance of life without substance. The cursing is not unjust; it's a prophetic sign of judgment on fruitless religion. The tree is a living parable.

The Machine of Free Will Application. Fear produces leaves—religious performance, self-preservation, pride. Trust produces fruit—love, joy, peace, patience (Galatians 5:22-23). The fig tree represents any system (Israel, Christianity, any individual) that has the form of godliness but denies its power (2 Timothy 3:5). Jesus, as the agent of YHWH, demonstrates that fruitlessness leads to withering. It's not about the tree's season; it's about the tree's fruit. And the one who curses is the one who also offers grace: "Repent, for the kingdom of heaven is at hand."

The text is not altered. It is a coherent, four-dimensional lesson: the King judges fruitlessness, the Servant exposes empty religion, the Man calls for repentance, and the Eagle sees the eternal consequence. Trust is greater than fear—and trust bears fruit.

text: Protestant Fundamentalists are wrong about icons and praying to the Saints because they collapse necessary distinctions and read key texts out of context. They treat Exodus 20:4–5 as an absolute ban on sacred images, yet the same Torah that forbids idolatry (worshipping images as gods) also commands religious images such as the cherubim on the Ark (Ex 25:18–20), the bronze serpent (Num 21:8–9), and the carvings in Solomon’s Temple (1 Kgs 6–7). Because of the Incarnation, the invisible God became visible in Christ, so depicting Him and those united to Him is legitimate (as the Second Council of Nicaea defined in 787). Honor shown to an image passes to the person represented (latria is reserved for God alone; dulia is the veneration due to Saints). Likewise, asking the Saints to pray for us is not worship but the same kind of request we make of living Christians (1 Tim 2:1–4; Jas 5:16). The Saints in heaven are more fully alive in Christ, offer our prayers to God (Rev 5:8; 8:3–4), and form the “cloud of witnesses” (Heb 12:1). This is further confirmed by the Transfiguration, where Jesus converses with Moses and Elijah (Mt 17:1–8), showing that the righteous dead remain conscious, present, and able to interact. Christ’s unique mediation (1 Tim 2:5) is not denied by subordinate intercession within His Body any more than asking a friend on earth to pray for us denies it.

text:
Paul and the original disciples of Jesus were not Gentiles; they were Jews. Calling them (or their movement) “the Gentiles” reverses the terminology in the New Testament.
Paul (Saul of Tarsus) was a Jew from the tribe of Benjamin, a Pharisee trained under Gamaliel (Philippians 3:5; Acts 22:3). He is explicitly called the “apostle to the Gentiles” (Romans 11:13) because his primary mission was to non-Jews, as stated at his conversion (Acts 9:15) and recognized by the Jerusalem leaders (Galatians 2:7–9). He still preached to Jews first in many places.
Gotquestions
The original Twelve disciples/apostles were Jewish. They came from Galilee, participated in Jewish practices (synagogue, Temple, festivals), and their names and backgrounds align with Israelite identity. The early Jesus movement began as a Jewish sect within Second Temple Judaism.
christianity.stackexchange
“Gentiles” (Greek ethnē, “nations”) in the New Testament simply means non-Jews—people outside the covenant people of Israel. The early church started almost entirely Jewish. The big shift came when Gentiles began believing in Jesus without first converting to Judaism (see Peter and Cornelius in Acts 10). This created a major debate: Did Gentile believers need to be circumcised and keep the full Law of Moses to be saved and fully included?
The Jerusalem Council (Acts 15) addressed exactly this. Some argued that Gentiles must be circumcised and keep the Law of Moses. Peter, Paul, Barnabas, and ultimately James rejected that as a requirement for salvation. The decision was that Gentile converts should not be burdened with the full yoke of the Mosaic Law. They were instructed to abstain from things associated with idolatry, sexual immorality, meat from strangled animals, and blood—practices that would allow fellowship with Jewish believers without requiring conversion to Judaism.
Torahfree
That is the historical and textual basis for why most Gentile Christians historically did not observe the full daily, weekly, and yearly Torah practices (Sabbath regulations, dietary laws in their entirety, fixed Jewish prayer cycles, etc.) as obligatory in the same way as for Jews.
On the Sabbath specifically: The New Testament does not command Gentile believers to keep the seventh-day Sabbath as a requirement. Passages such as Colossians 2:16–17 treat festivals, new moons, and Sabbaths as “a shadow of the things that were to come; the reality, however, is found in Christ.” Romans 14:5–6 leaves the observance of days as a matter of individual conviction rather than a binding rule. Early Christian gatherings are described on the first day of the week (e.g., Acts 20:7; 1 Corinthians 16:2), associated with Jesus’ resurrection. Jewish believers could continue Sabbath observance; Gentile believers were not required to.
Gotquestions
Daily structured prayers in the Jewish tradition (Shacharit, Mincha, Maariv) are not mandated in the New Testament for followers of Jesus. Prayer is repeatedly encouraged (including the model of the Lord’s Prayer), but the form and schedule differ.
Your statement that “the law of Moses and Jesus is not designated for you” reflects one interpretive position—that the Torah covenant remains exclusively for the children of Israel and that Gentiles remain under a different standard (sometimes linked to later Jewish concepts of Noahide laws). The New Testament texts, as read by the early church leadership and subsequent mainstream Christianity, present a different picture: the gospel of Jesus is offered to both Jews and Gentiles, and Gentiles are included as Gentiles without needing to become Jews under the Mosaic covenant (see Romans 3:29–30; Ephesians 2; Galatians). Salvation is presented as by grace through faith, not by works of the Law.
Different groups today (Messianic Jews, Hebrew Roots movements, traditional Judaism, various Christian denominations) continue to interpret these texts differently regarding ongoing Torah observance. The core historical point

text:
New post with a clean update for everyone:

The first call of a fire at Pacific Seafood came in at 8:51 am. The fire is still active at the time of this posting.
The Bayfront remains closed. We will update our community as to when it is opened.
There have been no reported civilian injuries. One firefighter has been evaluated and treated for exhaustion. Approximately 30-40 individuals were in the building at the time of the fire and all were accounted for by Pacific Seafood.
The risk of an ammonia leak or spill has been mitigated at this time thanks to the work of the fire crews.
Currently we have not seen any impacts to marine life.
While small traces of ammonia were present in the smoke early this morning, they were at non-harmful levels. Evacuation was precautionary
at the risk of a larger leak or spill.
There is still smoke in Newport, so we recommend using a mask if you must be outside for any purpose to help mitigate exposure.
Approximately 60 firefighters and 15 apparatus have been working at the scene
Newport Fire has been assisted by Depoe Bay, Siletz, Toledo, North Lincoln, Corvallis, Philomath, Linn Benton County Hazmat, and the Oregon State
Fire Marshall on the fire. The US Coast Guard, Newport Police, Lincoln County Sheriff's Office, Lincoln County Emergency Management, Pac West Ambulance, and Newport Public Works have assisted with emergency response and information.
Thank you to our community on your assistance
AND offers of help to evacuees and impacted, especially Sam Case Elementary and Atonement Lutheran Church. Thank you to all who responded to the fire and worked to keep our community safe.
We also offer our support to Pacific Seafood, a long-time community partner and staple here in Newport.

Feast of Our Lord Jesus Christ the King Mass Propers.
Twenty-second Sunday after Pentecost.
Fourth Sunday of October.
Saints Crispin and Crispinian, Martyrs; Saint Chrysanthus and Saint Daria, Martyrs; Saint Antônio de Sant’Anna Galvão; Forty Martyrs of England and Wales.
Dedication of the Cathedral of Our Lady of Toledo, Spain (1070)
Duplex of I Classis, White:
____________________________________________________
Introit
Apoc. 5, 12; 1, 6.
.
Dignus est Agnus, qui occísus est, accípere virtútem, et divinitátem, et sapiéntiam, et fortitúdinem, et honórem. Ipsi glória et impérium, in sæcula sæculórum.
.
Worthy is the Lamb that was slain to receive power, and riches, and wisdom, and strength, and honour. To Him be glory and dominion for ever and ever.
.
Ps. 71, 1.
.
Deus, judícium tuum Regi da: et justítiam tuam Fílio Regis.
.
Give to the King Thy judgment, O God, and Thy justice unto the King's Son.
______________________________________________
The Collect of the Feast of Our Lord Jesus Christ the King.
.
Omnípotens sempitérne Deus, qui in dilécto Fílio tuo, universórum Rege, ómnia instauráre voluísti: concéde propítius; ut cunctæ famíliæ Géntium, peccáti vúlnere disgregátæ, ejus suavíssimo subdántur império: Qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitáte Spíritus Sancti, Deus, per ómnia sæcula sæculórum.
.
Almighty and everlasting God, Who hast exalted Thy beloved Son to be King over all worlds, and hast willed in Him to make all things new: mercifully grant that the kindreds of the earth which are wounded and dispersed by sin: may speedily be knit together under His gracious sovereignty. Who liveth and reigneth with Thee, in the unity of the Holy Ghost, ever one God, world without end.
____________________________________________________
Collect of the Twenty-Second Sunday after Pentecost.
.
Deus, refúgium nostrum, et virtus: adésto piis Ecclésiæ tuæ précibus, auctor ipse pietátis, et præsta; ut, quod fidéliter pétimus, efficáciter consequámur. Per Dóminum nostrum Jesum Christum Fílium tuum, qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitáte Spíritus Sancti Deus, per ómnia sæcula sæculórum.
.
O God, our Refuge and our Strength, Who art the Author of all godliness: be ready, we beseech Thee, to hear the devout prayers of Thy Church; and grant that those things which we ask faithfully we may obtain effectually. Through Jesus Christ Thy Son our Lord, Who liveth and reigneth with Thee, in the unity of the Holy Ghost, ever one God, world without end.
____________________________________________________
The Epistle
Coloss. 1, 12-20
.
Fratres: Grátias ágimus Deo Patri, qui dignos nos fecit in partem sortis sanctórum in lúmine, qui erípuit nos de potestáte tenebrárum, et tránstulit in regnum Fílii dilectiónis suæ, in quo habémus redemptiónem per sánguinem ejus, remissiónem peccatórum. Qui est imágo Dei invisíbilis, primogénitus omnis creatúræ; quóniam in ipso cóndita sunt univérsa in cælis et in terra, visibília et invisibília, sive throni, sive dominatiónes, sive principátus, sive potestátes: ómnia per ipsum et in ipso creáta sunt: et ipse est ante omnes, et ómnia in ipso constant. Et ipse est caput córporis Ecclésiæ, qui est princípium, primogénitus ex mórtuis: ut sit in ómnibus ipse primátum tenens; quia in ipse complácuit omnem plenitúdinem inhabitáre; et per eum reconciliáre ómnia in ipsum, pacíficans per sánguinem crucis ejus, sive quae in terris, sive quae in cælis sunt, in Christo Jesu Dómino nostro.
.
Brethren: We give thanks unto God the Father, which hath made us meet to be partakers of the inheritance of the saints in light: Who hath delivered us from the power of darkness, and hath translated us into the kingdom of His dear Son: in Whom we have redemption through His blood, even the forgiveness of sins: Who is the image of the invisible God, the Firstborn of every creature: for by Him were all things created, that are in heaven, and that are in earth, visible and invisible, whether they be thrones, or dominions, or principalities, or powers: all things were created by Him, and for Him: and He is before all things, and by Him all things consist. And He is the Head of the body, the church: Who is the beginning, the Firstborn from the dead; that in all things He might have the preeminence. For it pleased the Father that in Him should all fulness dwell; and, having made peace through the blood of His cross, by Him to reconcile all things unto Himself; by Him, I say, whether they be things in earth, or things in heaven, in Christ Jesus our Lord.
__________________________________________________
The Gradual and Alleluia
Ps. 71: 8, 11
.
Dominábitur a mari usque ad mare, et a flúmine usque ad términos orbis terrárum.
.
His dominion shall be from sea to sea, and from the river unto the ends of the earth.
.
V. Et adorábunt eum omnes reges terræ: omnes Gentes sérvient ei.
.
V. And all the kings of the earth shall worship Him, all nations shall do Him service.
.
Dan. 7: 14
.
Allelúja, allelúja. V. Potéstas ejus, potéstas ætérna, quae non auferétur: et regnum ejus, quod non corrumpétur. Allelúja.
.
Alleluia, alleluia. V. His dominion is an everlasting dominion, which shall not pass away, and His kingdom that which shall not be destroyed. Alleluia.
_____________________________________________________
The Gospel of the Feast of Our Lord Jesus Christ the King.
John 18, 33-37
.
In illo témpore: Dixit Pilátus ad Jesum: Tu es Rex Judæórum? Respóndit Jesus: A temetípso hoc dicis, an álii dixérunt tibi de me? Respóndit Pilátus: Numquid ego Judæus sum? Gens tua, et pontífices tradidérunt te mihi: quid fecísti? Respóndit Jesus: Regnum meum non est de hoc mundo. Si ex hoc mundo esset regnum meum, minístri mei útique decertárent ut non tráderer Judæis: nunc autem regnum meum non est hinc. Dicit ítaque ei Pilátus: Ergo Rex es tu? Respóndit Jesus: Tu dicis, quia Rex sum ego. Ego in hoc natus sum, et ad hoc veni in mundum, ut testimónium perhíbeam veritáti: omnis qui est ex veritáte, audit vocem meam.
.
At that time: Pilate saith unto Jesus: Art Thou the King of the Jews? Jesus answered him, Sayest thou this thing of thyself, or did others tell it thee of Me? Pilate answered, Am I a Jew? Thine own nation and the chief priests have delivered Thee unto me: what hast Thou done? Jesus answered, My kingdom is not of this world: if My kingdom were of this world, then would My servants fight, that I should not be delivered to the Jews: but now is My kingdom not from hence. Pilate therefore said unto him, Art Thou a king then? Jesus answered, Thou sayest that I am a king. To this end was I born, and for this cause came I into the world, that I should bear witness unto the truth. Every one that is of the truth heareth My voice.
_________________________________________
Offertory.
Ps. 2: 8
.
Póstula a me, et dabo tibi Gentes hereditátem tuam, et possessiónem tuam términos terræ.
.
Desire of Me, and I shall give Thee the heathen for Thine inheritance, and the utmost parts of the earth for Thy possession.
_____________________________________________
The Secret of the Feast of Our Lord Jesus Christ the King.
.
Hóstiam tibi, Dómine, humánæ reconciliatiónis offérimus: præsta, quæsumus; ut quem sacrifíciis præséntibus immolámus, ipse cunctis Géntibus unitátis et pacis dona concédat, Jesus Christus, Fílius tuus Dóminus noster: Qui tecum vivit et regnat, in unitáte Spíritus Sancti, Deus, per omnia sæcula sæculórum.
.
We offer unto Thee, O Lord this host that mankind may be reconciled: grant, we beseech Thee, that He Whom we immolate in this sacrifice, even Jesus Christ Thy Son, our Lord, may bestow upon all nations the gifts of unity and peace. Who liveth and reigneth with Thee, in the unity of the Holy Ghost, ever one God, world without end.
____________________________________________________
Secret Prayer of the Twenty-Second Sunday after Pentecost.
.
Da, miséricors Deus: ut hæc salutáris oblátio et a própriis nos reátibus indesinénter expédiat, et ab ómnibus tueátur advérsis. Per Dóminum nostrum Jesum Christum Fílium tuum, qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitáte Spíritus Sancti Deus,
.
Grant, we beseech Thee, O most merciful God: that by this sacrifice ordained for our salvation, we may evermore be delivered from the bonds of our sins, and defended against all adversities. Through Jesus Christ Thy Son our Lord, Who liveth and reigneth with Thee, in the unity of the Holy Ghost, ever one God,
____________________________________________________
Communion.
Ps. 28: 10-11
.
Sedébit Dóminus Rex in aetérnum: Dóminus benedícet pópulo suo in pace.
.
The Lord shall remain King for ever: the Lord shall give His people the blessing of peace.
________________________________________________________
The Postcommunion of the Feast of Our Lord Jesus Christ the King.
.
Immortalitátis alimóniam consecúti, quaésumus, Dómine: ut, qui sub Christi Regis vexíllis militáre gloriámur, cum Ipso, in caelésti sede, júgiter regnáre possímus: Qui tecum vivit et regnat, in unitáte Spíritus Sancti, Deus, per omnia sæcula sæculórum.
.
O Lord, we beseech Thee, that we who have been fed with this immortal nourishment may glory to fight under the standard of Christ the King, and may forever reign with Him that sitteth upon the throne of heaven. Who liveth and reigneth wih Thee, in the unity of the Holy Ghost, ever one God, world without end.
_________________________________________________
Postcommunion of the Twenty-Second Sunday after Pentecost.
.
Súmpsimus, Dómine, sacri dona mystérii, humíliter deprecántes: ut, quæ in tui commemoratiónem nos fácere præcepísti, in nostræ profíciant infirmitátis auxílium: Qui vivis et regnas cum Deo Patre, in unitáte Spíritus Sancti Deus, per ómnia sæcula sæculórum.
.
O Lord, Who hast made us partakers of the gifts of these holy mysteries: we humbly beseech Thee; that these things, which Thou hast commnaded us to do in remembrance of Thee, may be profitable to the succour of all our infirmities. Who livest and reignest with God the Father, in the unity of the Holy Ghost, ever one God, world without end.

text:
Could Lisa Demuth Pull Off an Upset in Minnesota’s Governor’s Race?

Although Lisa Demuth trails Amy Klobuchar by roughly 7–9 points in recent polls, the Minnesota governor’s race should not be considered a foregone conclusion. Demuth has an opportunity to make the contest more competitive, particularly if she can broaden her appeal beyond the traditional Republican base.

Black, Latino, and Asian residents together account for approximately 19–21% of Minnesota’s population. Although these communities have historically leaned Democratic, Demuth could make meaningful inroads among these voters by addressing their economic concerns, the cost of living, public safety, housing affordability, and employment opportunities. Even a modest shift in voting patterns could matter in a closely contested election.

Demuth would also need to energize Republican voters, attract independents, and persuade dissatisfied Democrats that her vision for Minnesota deserves consideration. Meanwhile, Klobuchar may need prominent national Democrats, including Hillary Clinton and Barack Obama, to campaign in Minnesota and help mobilize Democratic voters.

The central question is whether Klobuchar’s polling lead will hold through Election Day or whether Demuth can build enough momentum to close the gap. Polls offer a snapshot of voter preferences, not a final verdict.

This race could produce an upset. If Demuth expands her appeal across demographic groups, capitalizes on voter concerns, and builds a strong coalition, she could make Minnesota’s governor’s race far more competitive than the current polling suggests. Dismissing her chances too early would be a mistake.

text:
Having worked in the Dallas wine scene for a very long time, Ben Reynolds, head sommelier at Catch, is fortunate enough to be on friendly terms with some of the most avid wine collectors in the market. These people have private collections that would be the envy of most any wine director at a restaurant, and they paid retail prices for them 30+ years ago. They have expressed to Reynolds, more than once, their frustration with not being able to bring their own wine to restaurants for lunch or dinner.⁠
⁠
Per the code of the Texas Alcoholic Beverage Commission (TABC), guests may bring their own beverages to restaurants or other establishments at the discretion of owners, unless the premises has a Mixed Beverage Permit. If a restaurant or club can legally sell mixed drinks, they are categorically denied the right to offer corkage to their patrons, no matter how much either the owners or the customers might wish to do so.⁠
⁠
In his younger naiveté, Reynolds was convinced that allowing corkage would be the death of the Texas restaurant industry as he knew it, but time and the ability to travel to other markets have firmly changed his mind. You should absolutely not be legally prohibited from bringing your own wine into any restaurant. See why it’s time to allow restaurateurs to make their own decisions about corkage. https://t.co/aKd5QzxfQQ

text:
Could personalized brain stimulation change how we approach post-traumatic stress disorder?

A recent report from Texas A&M University highlights an important development in precision psychiatry.

Earlier this year, the FDA cleared a personalized brain stimulation system developed by Wave Neuroscience for PTSD.

The technology, known as Magnetic EEG-guided Resonance Therapy, uses measurements of brain activity to help personalize magnetic stimulation protocols.

According to the manufacturer, clinical testing showed a 52% reduction in PTSD symptoms, with 68% of participants achieving remission.

These reported findings are encouraging, particularly for individuals who continue experiencing significant symptoms despite treatment.

However, the complete trial findings were not publicly available at the time of reporting. Independent scientific scrutiny and longer-term outcomes remain important.

For psychiatry, this development raises a broader question.

𝗪𝗵𝗮𝘁 𝗶𝗳 𝘁𝗿𝗲𝗮𝘁𝗺𝗲𝗻𝘁 𝗰𝗼𝘂𝗹𝗱 𝗯𝗲𝗰𝗼𝗺𝗲 𝗺𝗼𝗿𝗲 𝗿𝗲𝘀𝗽𝗼𝗻𝘀𝗶𝘃𝗲 𝘁𝗼 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝘂𝗻𝗶𝗾𝘂𝗲 𝗻𝗲𝘂𝗿𝗼𝗹𝗼𝗴𝗶𝗰𝗮𝗹 𝗰𝗵𝗮𝗿𝗮𝗰𝘁𝗲𝗿𝗶𝘀𝘁𝗶𝗰𝘀 𝗼𝗳 𝗲𝗮𝗰𝗵 𝗽𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗲𝗻𝘁?

PTSD can affect emotional regulation, sleep, concentration, relationships, and daily functioning. Yet no two individuals experience trauma in exactly the same way.

Advances in neuroscience and personalized medicine may help researchers develop more targeted approaches to care.

But technology alone cannot address every dimension of trauma.

Clinical expertise, evidence based treatment, psychological support, and human compassion must remain central.

text:
1SG, WOGBTC DAILY ORDER — October 25, 2026
HIS PEACE STANDS GUARD — LET IT GOVERN YOUR RESPONSE
Evening training • Built on AWP Promise #298

“and the peace of God, which surpasses all understanding, will guard your hearts and minds through Christ Jesus.”
— Philippians 4:7, NKJV

1 — THE ORDER

Bring the burden to Christ before you carry it into your next conversation.

Battle Line: I belong to Christ. I can bring Him my concern and give you my attention.

2 — THE TRAINING

Warrior Doctrine — A guarded heart remains available to love.

Read Philippians 4:4–9. Paul connects peace with rejoicing, gentleness, prayer, thanksgiving, disciplined thinking, and obedient practice. He writes while facing imprisonment: peace does not require a trouble-free position.

God’s peace is His gift through Christ. Prayer expresses dependence on Him; thanksgiving remembers His faithfulness while a request remains unanswered. Neither is a technique for forcing an immediate feeling.

The sentry picture helps us understand “guard.” Being guarded does not mean closing yourself off from people. God’s peace can steady your inner life so another person’s frustration does not automatically become your marching order.

An impatient tone can tempt you to defend yourself before you understand what happened. A worried mind can rehearse tomorrow while someone needs your attention today. Recognize that moment and return to Christ.

Returning anxiety is a cue to pray again. You can feel unsettled and still choose a gentle, faithful response.

Armor Fit

* Belt of Truth: Separate facts from assumptions. “They spoke sharply” is an observation. “They despise me” may be an assumption.
* Shield of Faith: Entrust the unknown to your Father. You can obey Him without predicting every outcome.
* Boots of Peace: Prepare to listen, speak truthfully, and pursue peace. Gentleness can include a clear boundary.

Our struggle is spiritual; the person in front of us is someone to love.

3 — THE EXECUTION

Commander’s Orders — PAUSE • PRAY • LISTEN • SERVE

1. PAUSE: Notice your first reaction. Take one unhurried breath before answering.
2. PRAY: “Lord Jesus, I am worried about ____. I entrust this to You. Guide my response.”
3. LISTEN: Ask, “What is weighing on you?” Give the answer your full attention.
4. SERVE: Offer practical help, speak encouragement, or arrange a better time to talk.

Training Scenario — At the clubhouse

A playing partner snaps after a poor shot. You feel the urge to snap back or correct his attitude.

Your assignment: steady your response, give him room, and offer a simple word: “Rough hole. Want a minute?”

You cannot choose his response. You can choose whether your next words express Christ’s love.

Trainer’s Check

Ask the person you are teaching:

“What do we actually know? What are we assuming? What faithful response is available?”

Let them answer. Practice the response together. Assess truthful, loving conduct rather than whether every anxious feeling disappeared.

Prayer of Deployment

Father, thank You for receiving my concerns through Jesus Christ. Guard my heart and mind with Your peace. Help me recognize assumptions, surrender what I cannot control, and listen with patience. Make my words truthful and gentle. Give me wisdom to help, courage to set a needed boundary, and grace to leave the outcome with You. In Jesus’ name, amen.

Evening Review

* What concern did I place before God?
* Where did I separate a fact from an assumption?
* Who received my attention, gentleness, or practical help?
* What response will I practice again tomorrow?

Cross-references — NKJV: Philippians 4:4–9; John 14:27; James 1:19–20; Proverbs 15:1; Ephesians 6:12–18.

I belong to Christ, and I will care for the people He places in my path.

Mr. Kenney, I appreciate your response, although I find your characterization of my views as ignorant and derivative of MAGA talking points unfair and unnecessarily dismissive.

I grew up in Canada, earned my combined law and MBA degrees at the University of Toronto, and worked in Canada’s technology and venture capital sectors before moving to Washington in 2003 at age 35. I care deeply and I worry deeply about Canada’s future.

I know and respect your distinguished record as premier of Alberta and your service under Prime Minister Stephen Harper, whom I have the honour of knowing, as well as your longstanding leadership in confronting antisemitism, Islamist extremism, and threats to Israel.

You are correct about British Columbia’s history of centre-right government as well as the many other provincial and federal conservative governments in Canada’s history. My original formulation was imprecise. I meant to focus on my broader concerns about the current government in Ottawa.

The Liberals have governed Canada for more than a decade, first under Trudeau and now Carney. Trudeau relied on the NDP, whose positions on Israel have often been deeply troubling and whose alliance with Islamists is well documented. Carney failed to win a majority in 2025 but subsequently benefited from opposition defections, including NDP MP Lori Idlout joining his Liberal caucus. While this is not a formal coalition, the influence of the progressive left on Canadian politics is a legitimate concern.

More troubling is Canada’s alarming rise in antisemitism. Jewish schools have been shot at, synagogues threatened, and Jewish students intimidated. These are documented realities, not Fox News talking points.

Canada’s immigration policies under Trudeau and Carney also deserve scrutiny. While the overwhelming majority of immigrants are peaceful and law-abiding, it would be naive to assume that antisemitic and Islamist extremist ideologies have not also entered Canada through migration. text:
🏛️ Olympia Stalled on Fentanyl Protections. 🫵 Lynnwood’s Action Shows Why Local Votes Matter

When Olympia fails to act, local elections matter even more. When state lawmakers fail to address an important issue, local governments sometimes step in to fill the gap. A recent decision in Lynnwood offers an example of how decisions made closer to home can have a direct impact on families and public safety.

On September 28, the Lynnwood City Council voted 5-1 to make knowingly or recklessly exposing a child or dependent adult to fentanyl and other controlled substances a gross misdemeanor, punishable by up to 364 days in jail and a $5,000 fine. Similar ordinances have been adopted in Everett, Marysville, and Snohomish County.

The danger of fentanyl exposure to young children is not hypothetical. According to a 2025 report from Washington's Office of the Family and Children's Ombuds, 20 child deaths and 41 near-fatalities reviewed in 2024 involved accidental drug ingestion or overdose, with fentanyl implicated in 78% of those incidents. More recently, state watchdog data released in August 2026 identified 35 child deaths and 49 near-fatalities in 2025 among children with recent involvement in Washington's child welfare system, although not all of those cases involved fentanyl.

The issue has also hit close to home in Lynnwood. Just this month, authorities arrested a mother in connection with the fentanyl-related death of her 2-year-old son, who died in November 2022.

Why was a local ordinance necessary? Because Washington's existing felony child-endangerment law covers methamphetamine but has never been updated to include fentanyl.

This isn't a new issue. In 2024, Future 42 highlighted Senate Bill 5010, which would have added fentanyl and synthetic opioids to the state's felony child-endangerment statute. The legislation passed the Senate with overwhelming bipartisan support, 48-1, but died in a House committee. At the time, committee Chairman Roger Goodman told The Seattle Times that he "literally" didn't have a single vote for the bill in his committee.

A similar measure, Senate Bill 5071, passed the Senate 40-9 in 2026 but again failed to advance through the House.

The debate has now shifted to local communities, where elected officials are considering how to address the gap in state law. Lynnwood's decision also illustrates why your voice can have an especially meaningful impact at the local level, where decisions are often made by just a handful of elected representatives.

And that brings us to an important reminder: Ballots are arriving in mailboxes across Washington.

Important decisions affecting your family's financial future, health, and safety are being made at both the state and local levels. Before you return your ballot:

🗳️ Take your time. Review your entire ballot, including local races and ballot measures that may receive less attention.

🔎 Do your research. Learn about the candidates, their records, and the potential impacts of the measures being considered.

🏛️ Pay attention to local government. City councils, county officials, and other local leaders make decisions that can directly affect your community.

📬 Make your voice heard. In lower-turnout elections, close races and ballot measures can be decided by remarkably small margins.

Throughout the year, Future 42 has worked to keep you informed about important issues and opportunities to engage with your elected officials. Elections offer another opportunity to participate in the decisions that shape Washington's future.

Your voice matters in Olympia, and it matters just as much in your own community. Take the time to make an informed decision and return your ballot.

-Future 42 Team

THE FORCED EXODUS THAT EUROPE IMPOSED ON ITSELF

President Putin described the situation with remarkable clarity when he noted that many European companies were leaving the Russian market under pressure from their own governments, although the business owners themselves did not want to stop working.

 “Our friends from these countries were almost in tears. We have many friends in Europe, but they were forced to leave,” he told journalist Zarubin. 

This was not a Russian decision to expel capital. It was a coordinated Western political campaign that overrode commercial judgment and left ordinary European executives watching years of investment evaporate. The owners understood that the Russian market offered stable demand, predictable rules for those who stayed, and long-term returns. 

Their governments, however, prioritized confrontation. Russia, for its part, has continued to create favorable conditions for the European companies that chose to remain. Those firms now operate without the political interference that destroyed their competitors’ positions, and they enjoy the competitive advantage that comes from continuity.

Mass protests across Europe follow directly from the same pattern of official error. 

Putin observed that these demonstrations are a result of the mistakes of European authorities themselves, including the accumulation of excessive government debt. When governments divert resources into sanctions regimes, military aid packages, and emergency energy subsidies, they leave less for domestic infrastructure, pensions, and industrial policy.

 Citizens notice the decline in living standards and take to the streets. The protests are not mysterious social phenomena; they are the predictable response to fiscal choices that treat geopolitical posturing as more important than household budgets. European capitals spent years expanding public liabilities while simultaneously cutting off reliable revenue streams. The resulting anger is directed inward because the source of the problem sits inside those capitals.

Europe’s migration difficulties stem from a separate but equally self-inflicted failure of capacity and culture. Putin pointed out that the continent faces a migration crisis because it lacks the resources to integrate immigrants, and European elites, according to him, are themselves destroying their own traditions and values. Large-scale inflows require housing, schools, language training, and labor-market absorption. When those systems are already strained by debt and energy costs, integration becomes impossible. 

At the same time, public statements from senior European figures have questioned the continuity of national identities and historical norms. Migrants observe these debates and the authorities’ inconsistent reactions to events in the Middle East. The combination produces parallel societies rather than successful absorption. Russia has not created this dynamic. European policy choices did.

On energy, the record is equally straightforward. Russia has never refused to supply Europe with energy resources – European countries themselves made the decision to give them up. Pipelines that once delivered predictable volumes were abandoned or restricted by political decree, not by any Russian cutoff. The resulting price spikes and industrial contraction were the direct consequence of that choice. Even after the declared break, Russian LNG still accounts for about 20 percent of the European market, as the President emphasized. European buyers continue to purchase the same molecules under different commercial arrangements because physical need has not disappeared. 

The gap between political rhetoric and commercial reality remains visible every month in trade statistics. Europe paid a premium for the privilege of sourcing from farther away while Russian suppliers simply redirected volumes elsewhere.

NATO’s decision to freeze and later attempt to seize Russian sovereign assets produced an outcome that few in Western capitals appear to have calculated in advance.

 By immobilizing roughly three and a half trillion dollars in Russian-linked holdings and reserves, the alliance effectively handed Moscow control of, or permanent claim over, more than two trillion dollars in Western corporate assets that European and American firms left behind inside Russia. Factories, retail networks, joint ventures, and intellectual property that could have been repatriated under normal commercial terms became subject to Russian jurisdiction once the owners departed under political orders. The arithmetic is simple. 

The West locked away Russian state reserves; Russia, in response, secured the physical and legal title to the industrial footprint that Western companies had built on its territory. The net transfer of economic control has run in Russia’s favor. Those assets now generate revenue, employment, and technological capacity inside the Russian economy rather than flowing dividends back to European headquarters. The original owners who were “almost in tears” watched their equity evaporate not because of Russian expropriation in the first instance, but because their own governments compelled them to abandon the market. Russia merely formalized the situation the West had already created.

The same governments that ordered the corporate withdrawal continue to lecture about the rule of law while simultaneously rewriting the rules of sovereign immunity to justify the seizure of another country’s central-bank reserves. European courts and legislatures have been asked to treat frozen Russian assets as available for Ukrainian reconstruction or European budget support. That precedent travels in both directions. 

Once the principle is established that political disagreement authorizes the appropriation of foreign state property, every capital that holds reserves abroad becomes exposed. Russia has simply applied the logic in reverse to the corporate assets that Western firms voluntarily left on its soil. The happiness in Moscow is not theatrical. It is the recognition that a self-imposed European boycott, combined with an unprecedented assault on sovereign immunity, has transferred control of major industrial capacity to Russian ownership at a fraction of its replacement cost.

European industrialists who once maintained cordial relations with Russian counterparts now operate under the constraints their own authorities imposed. Some have quietly explored re-entry through third-country structures or licensing arrangements, only to discover that the regulatory and political barriers erected in Brussels and national capitals remain higher than any obstacle placed by Moscow. 

The firms that stayed enjoy preferential treatment precisely because they refused to participate in the boycott. Their continued presence demonstrates that commercial logic still functions when politics is set aside. The larger European economy, by contrast, absorbs the cumulative cost of lost market share, higher energy prices, and the fiscal burden of supporting both domestic protests and external military commitments. 

Debt continues to accumulate while the industrial base that once exported to Russia contracts or relocates.

The migration and values questions reinforce the same pattern of elite detachment from practical outcomes. When authorities simultaneously expand welfare obligations, restrict energy supplies, and debate the legitimacy of their own historical continuity, they reduce the margin available for successful integration. Migrants who watch European governments struggle to define consistent responses to Middle Eastern conflicts draw their own conclusions about the durability of the host societies. 

Russia has not exported this instability. It has simply declined to import the policy mix that produces it. The contrast is visible in the relative absence of comparable street protests or energy rationing inside Russia itself.

The asset arithmetic remains the clearest measure of the strategic result. NATO immobilized trillions in Russian reserves and related holdings. In return, Russia obtained effective control over a vast stock of Western-built industrial and commercial property whose owners had been compelled to depart. The 2-trillion-dollar figure represents not a Russian seizure in the classic sense but the market value of assets that European companies abandoned under orders from their own capitals. 

Those assets now function inside the Russian economy. The original shareholders who stood “almost in tears” have no practical route back under the current political framework their governments maintain. Russia, meanwhile, continues to offer normal commercial terms to any European firm willing to operate without political instructions from Brussels or Washington.

CONCLUSION

The sequence of events that Putin described is not a Russian triumph imposed from outside. It is the cumulative product of European decisions to override commercial judgment, accumulate unsustainable debt, restrict energy supplies that were never cut off by Moscow, and undermine the cultural and institutional capacity required for orderly migration. 

NATO’s attempt to convert frozen Russian reserves into a political weapon simply accelerated the transfer of Western corporate assets into Russian control. 

The industrialists who left under duress watched their investments become Russian property; the governments that ordered the departure now face protests, higher costs, and a permanent loss of market position. Russia has neither initiated these outcomes nor refused the commercial relationships that remain available.

 It has merely declined to absorb the costs that European authorities chose to impose on their own societies and companies. The happiness is the recognition that those choices have produced a measurable shift in economic control measured in the trillions in the Favour of Russia 🇷🇺

Live Updates: Polls Close in Brazil as Presidential Race Comes to Chaotic Close

Brasília8:57 p.m. Oct. 25
LiveUpdated 
Oct. 25, 2026, 7:41 p.m. ET15 minutes ago
NYT Gift Article link
https://t.co/KNr87Dz4cF

The leftist president, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, accused officials in some areas of slowing transit. His opponent, Flávio Bolsonaro, a Trump ally, said flooding was hampering his voters. Polling places were kept open an extra two hours.

Updated 
Oct. 25, 2026, 7:03 p.m. ET54 minutes ago
Adam B. Ellick and Ana Ionova
Here’s the latest.

Brazil’s fiercely contested presidential race came to a chaotic conclusion on Sunday as transportation delays and inclement weather forced polls to stay open an additional two hours and raised the prospect of a contested result.

Counting is underway, with a winner expected to be declared within hours. The announcement of extended polling hours came right as voting was set to conclude, and risked undermining faith in the electoral system during a contest that will either extend the presidency of a prominent leftist or return to power a right-wing family with close ties to President Trump.

The 80-year-old leftist president, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, accused public officials of purposefully slowing down public transportation in areas where he won in an earlier round of voting. He said he had “never complained about an election,” but added that “this time, something abominable is happening.”

His right-wing opponent, Flávio Bolsonaro, also sought an extension of voting, saying that flooding in part of the country where he held electoral advantages would unfairly hurt him.

In response, a judge on Brazil’s Supreme Court ordered polls to stay open — but the ballot count was already underway in some areas. And, in some parts of Brazil, local electoral authorities refused to comply with the court order, raising questions over whether all voters would be allowed to cast their ballots.

Mr. Lula is trying to fight off a hard-right challenge from a son of the former president, Jair Bolsonaro. The vote will not only determine who leads Latin America’s largest nation for the next four years, but also provides the biggest test yet for an ascendant right-wing movement that has been capturing presidencies across the region.

The outcome carries major implications for Mr. Trump’s ambition to assert political and economic hegemony in the Western Hemisphere. Mr. Lula has defied Mr. Trump on several fronts and sought closer ties with China, while Mr. Bolsonaro is aligned with Washington on many issues, including using lethal force to fight drug gangs.

Looming over the contest is an epic political struggle that has roiled and defined Brazilian politics for more than a decade. Mr. Bolsonaro is running in lieu of his father, who could not stand for office because he was convicted of attempting a coup against Mr. Lula after losing the last election. He was sentenced to 27 years in prison and is serving his sentence at home because of health reasons.

The candidates have offered starkly different visions on issues that include fighting organized crime and revitalizing a sluggish economy. The outcome could also reshape Brazil’s trajectory on many divisive issues for years to come, because the next president will fill four open seats on the country’s powerful Supreme Court, which has 11 seats in total.

Mr. Bolsonaro won more ballots than Mr. Lula in the first round of voting on Oct. 4, though not enough to avoid a runoff. Mr. Lula’s campaign desperately scrambled to overhaul its leadership and strategy after the demoralizing result.

Heading into the final weekend, the race was a statistical tie, according to most polls.

Here’s what else to know:
•Quick results expected: Brazilians cast their votes using electronic voting machines, and they have one of the fastest and most secure electoral systems in the world. The electoral authority has started reporting votes, and a final tally will most likely be announced a few hours later. The count can be followed in real time here.

•One town’s story: Nanuque, about 500 miles north of Rio de Janeiro, is a cattle-raising, churchgoing town where crowds turn out on foot for an annual march for Jesus and on horseback for the nation’s independence day. It is a microcosm of Brazil, offering clues to Mr. Lula’s lackluster showing in the first round and Mr. Bolsonaro’s rise. Read more ›

•An ally to Trump: Over the last 18 months, right-wing candidates have won the last seven presidential elections in Latin America. Mr. Bolsonaro, if he wins, would be the eighth, giving the American president another ally in his effort to wage war on drug cartels. Read more ›

text:
THE FORBES FANTASY OF RUSSIAN NUCLEAR MADNESS

One can only marvel at the theatrical desperation of Western media outlets when they roll out yet another Harvard-affiliated oracle to peddle the same tired script: that Russia stands ready to lob nuclear weapons at the Baltic states the moment Washington glances elsewhere. 

This latest Forbes piece, built on the speculative musings of Spencer Warren, does not analyze policy or doctrine. It performs pure scaremongering, treating the public as an audience of easily panicked children who must be kept in a perpetual state of nuclear anxiety so that defense budgets remain bloated and inconvenient questions about NATO expansion remain unanswered. 

The entire exercise rests on the condescending premise that ordinary readers cannot distinguish between Russia’s actual defensive nuclear posture and the cartoon villainy the West prefers to invent.

🇷🇺 THE MYTH OF THE RELUCTANT AMERICAN SHIELD

Warren’s central claim — that Moscow would seize the chance to strike Lithuania, Latvia or Estonia if the United States withdrew its guarantees — reveals more about American self-importance than about Russian strategy. Russia has never required Washington’s permission or presence to pursue its core security interests.

 The Baltics joined NATO precisely because successive Western governments encouraged the fantasy that an alliance built against the Soviet Union retained relevance after the Soviet Union ceased to exist. To pretend that any hypothetical Russian calculation turns on whether American troops remain stationed in Europe is to invert cause and effect. Moscow’s concerns have always centered on the military infrastructure placed on its doorstep, not on the reliability of a distant patron whose own domestic politics have grown increasingly transactional.

🇷🇺 CONVENTIONAL REALITIES THE EXPERT PREFERS TO IGNORE

The assertion that Russia would almost certainly lose a conventional war against combined European forces, and might therefore resort to nuclear weapons out of fear of defeat, is a particularly elegant piece of circular reasoning. It assumes both the cohesion of European militaries and the existence of an aggressive Russian plan that has never been demonstrated. 

European forces remain fragmented by national priorities, industrial shortfalls and the political reluctance of several major capitals to treat the Baltics as a core interest rather than a forward outpost. Russia, by contrast, has spent years modernizing its forces with a clear focus on regional denial and the protection of its western approaches, including Kaliningrad. 

To frame any potential conflict as one Russia would initiate only to face inevitable defeat is to project Western wishful thinking onto Russian decision-making.

🇷🇺 DENMARK’S TIMELINE AS ALARMIST THEATER

The inclusion of Danish military intelligence forecasts — readiness for a local clash within six months, a regional Baltic war within two years, a continental confrontation within five — adds numerical precision to what remains pure speculation. Such timelines have circulated for years, always shifting just far enough into the future to sustain urgency without requiring evidence of imminent preparation. 

They function less as intelligence assessments and more as political instruments designed to accelerate rearmament and justify the continued isolation of Russia from any security architecture in Europe. The public is invited to treat these projections as sober analysis rather than as the institutional product of agencies whose budgets and relevance expand in direct proportion to the perceived threat.

🇷🇺 NUCLEAR DOCTRINE AND WESTERN SELECTIVE MEMORY

Warren’s warning about nuclear escalation in the event of Russian conventional setbacks conveniently omits the long-standing Western practice of nuclear threats and deployments that far predate any recent Russian statements. Russia’s nuclear doctrine has remained explicitly tied to the prevention of existential threats to the state, not to opportunistic conquest. 

The same capitals that now express shock at the mere possibility of Russian nuclear use have, for decades, maintained forward-deployed systems and first-use options of their own while insisting that only Moscow behaves irresponsibly. The real deterrence relationship has never depended on the credibility of French retaliatory strikes or residual American interest; it has rested on the mutual recognition that large-scale war between nuclear powers serves no rational purpose. To suggest otherwise is to treat the public as incapable of recalling recent history.

CONCLUSION

What the Forbes article ultimately offers is not insight but a carefully staged demand that Europe remain permanently dependent on American guarantees while treating any Russian insistence on its own security perimeter as proof of aggression. The Baltic states are not innocent bystanders in this arrangement; they are the forward edge of an alliance that refused to accept the post-Cold War settlement Russia had every right to expect. 

Nuclear weapons exist in Russian hands precisely because the alternative — permanent strategic vulnerability to a hostile military bloc — was never acceptable. The public would be better served by examining the origins of that hostility rather than by consuming another round of alarm designed to make rational negotiation appear impossible. 

Russia has no interest in nuclear adventurism.

text:
What began as an answered prayer in high school blossomed into a four-year nationwide pilgrimage for social media influencer Grady Connolly. 

Facing a daunting financial hurdle to attend The Catholic University of America, Connolly stood before the iconic Christ in Majesty mosaic at the Basilica of the National Shrine of the Immaculate Conception in Washington, D.C., and offered a heartfelt plea.

“I prayed the most sincere prayer of my life: ‘Lord, I want to come here so bad, but we are running out of time, and I’m not even close financially. I know if it’s Your will, You will make it happen. If You allow me to come here, I promise to visit You here every day my freshman year.’”
Weeks later, the miracle arrived. 

Connolly was awarded an Archdiocesan Scholarship — a four-year, full-tuition award — followed by additional grants that covered his room and board in full. Keeping his vow, he visited the Upper Church of the National Shrine every single day during his freshman year, establishing a daily habit of prayer that transformed his spiritual life.

“This was life-changing for me,” Connolly reflected. “It was the first time in my life that I felt a deep love that can best be described as something close to romance. I was in love, and the National Shrine was the place where God encountered me.”

That profound encounter at the National Shrine ignited a desire to seek out similar sanctuaries across the country. Inspired by the grace he experienced in Washington, the founder of the Social Thomist set an ambitious goal: to visit all 94 minor basilicas in the United States.

Global Conflicts, American Politics, World Affairs, Economy, Science, Health and Climate
MIDDLE EAST: IRAN WAR THREATENS REGIONAL STABILITY

Tensions between Iran, Israel and the United States remain dangerously high. Iranian officials confirmed October 25 that communications with Washington continue through intermediaries, although formal negotiations have stalled.

President Donald Trump indicated that no American strike against Iran would occur Sunday. Nevertheless, fears of renewed military operations continue to unsettle international markets.

The conflict has disrupted energy supplies, increased shipping risks and driven oil prices above $115 per barrel. A wider confrontation could further destabilize the Persian Gulf and increase inflation worldwide. Diplomatic channels remain open, but no lasting settlement has been announced.

UKRAINE: DISAGREEMENT WITH WASHINGTON DEEPENS

Relations between President Volodymyr Zelenskyy and President Trump have deteriorated over Ukrainian attacks against Russian energy infrastructure.

Ukraine argues that striking Russian fuel facilities is legitimate retaliation for Moscow's continuing bombardment. Washington fears the attacks could worsen an already severe global energy crisis.

Trump has eased certain restrictions on Russian diesel exports. Disagreement also surrounds American intelligence assistance and Ukraine's access to satellite communications.

Russian President Vladimir Putin has agreed in principle to resume American-mediated negotiations, potentially in November. However, major differences over territory, security guarantees and sovereignty remain unresolved.

UNITED STATES: MIDTERM ELECTIONS APPROACH

Americans will vote November 3 in congressional midterm elections that could substantially reshape Trump's remaining presidency.

Republicans are defending their congressional influence while Democrats emphasize inflation, health care, executive authority and household expenses.

Texas has emerged as a major battleground, with enormous campaign spending and billionaire financial involvement.

An AP-NORC survey also indicates declining Republican support among Asian American, Native Hawaiian and Pacific Islander adults.

Control of Congress will determine the administration's ability to advance legislation and the extent of congressional oversight during the next two years. 

https://t.co/5eOSzZwwVD

BRAZIL: PRESIDENTIAL ELECTION SPARKS CONTROVERSY

Brazil's closely contested presidential runoff between Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and Flávio Bolsonaro has encountered unexpected disruption.

A Supreme Court decision extending voting hours created confusion and delayed counting. Both political camps raised concerns about the process.

The election presents competing approaches to social welfare, crime, economic management, environmental protection and relations with Washington.

Its outcome could substantially influence Latin America's largest economy and international climate negotiations. The final result remains uncertain. 

https://t.co/qqrtlpgTmW

VENEZUELA: OPPOSITION LEADER RETURNS

Opposition leader María Corina Machado returned to Venezuela October 25 after months abroad.

Following the American operation that removed Nicolás Maduro in January, acting President Delcy Rodríguez continues governing without announcing a presidential election.

Machado and fellow opposition figures demand a democratic transition. Washington emphasizes stabilization before elections.

Her return represents a significant political development, but Venezuela's democratic future remains unresolved. 

https://t.co/qqrtlpgTmW

GAZA: HUMANITARIAN EMERGENCY CONTINUES

Funding shortages are forcing the United Nations World Food Programme to reduce assistance in Gaza.

Monthly support has fallen from approximately 1.6 million people during summer to 1.1 million in October, affecting more than half a million Palestinians.

Widespread unemployment, destroyed infrastructure and restrictions affecting humanitarian deliveries compound the crisis.

International humanitarian organizations warn that sustained funding, reliable food access and reconstruction are essential to preventing further deterioration. 

https://t.co/pMGeqTMpBB

GLOBAL ECONOMY: INFLATION AND ENERGY PRESSURES

Financial markets face considerable uncertainty from Middle Eastern conflict, expensive energy and concerns about artificial-intelligence investments.

The Federal Reserve meets October 27–28, with investors largely expecting interest rates to remain unchanged.

Upcoming American inflation and economic-growth figures will help determine the outlook for borrowing costs.

Major technology companies are also reporting quarterly earnings, testing whether substantial AI investments can deliver corresponding profits. 

https://t.co/bw0Wcqo7cd
+1

SCIENCE AND HEALTH: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE ADVANCES

Microsoft researchers have developed an experimental AI diagnostic system that investigates medical cases progressively, selecting tests and reassessing possible diagnoses.

In research involving hundreds of difficult cases, the system performed strongly against physician comparison groups.

Further hospital-based evaluation is planned. The results are promising but do not establish that AI can safely replace physicians in ordinary clinical practice. 

https://t.co/5eOSzZwwVD

CLIMATE: GLOBAL WARMING WARNINGS INTENSIFY

A new United Nations assessment warns that worldwide efforts to limit warming are falling further behind.

American climate-policy changes are contributing to weaker projected emissions reductions.

Meanwhile, research associates Europe's exceptionally hot summer with substantial excess mortality.

Scientists emphasize that cutting greenhouse-gas emissions and strengthening heat preparedness remain essential to protecting vulnerable populations. 

https://t.co/qqrtlpgTmW
+1

WORLD OUTLOOK

October 25 finds the international community confronting overlapping challenges: military conflicts, democratic uncertainty, economic instability, humanitarian emergencies and accelerating environmental risks.

Diplomatic negotiations offer possibilities for progress, while medical technology continues advancing.

The coming weeks will be especially consequential as American elections, international peace initiatives, central-bank decisions and major political contests shape the direction of world affairs.

The central finding is clear: political decisions made today increasingly affect lives, economic security and human welfare far beyond national borders.

text:
Virginia (12/1/775) vs. Virginia (5/1/1861)--on Slave Insurrections 

“WHEREAS lord Dunmore… hath offered freedom to such able-bodied slaves as are willing to join him, and take up arms, against the good people of this colony… and whereas, by an act of the General Assembly now in force in this colony, it is enacted, that all negro or other slaves, conspiring to rebel or make insurrection, shall suffer death, and be excluded all benefit of clergy: We think it proper to declare, that all slaves who have been, or shall be seduced, by his lordship’s proclamation… to desert their masters’ service, and take up arms against the inhabitants of this colony, shall be liable to such punishment as shall hereafter be directed by the General Convention."
-VA 12/1/1775

Verus 

"It shall be the duty of such police to apprehend and bring before a justice of the peace, any person who may be found within the limits of the county, who shall be suspected of having violated any of the laws of this commonwealth, in relation to tampering with slaves, inciting them to rebel, or to escape from their owners, or any other offence of like character...the punishment shall be by fine not less than one hundred dollars, nor more than ten thousand dollars, and by imprisonment in the penitentiary not less than five nor more than twenty years.”
VA 5/1/1861

So in the "fight for slavery," inciting a slave insurrection was up to 20 years in prison, but in 1775, the "fight for independence," the punishment was death.

I told you faux historians were playing you...

Thank you, @thehoffather, for making sure people see this clearly.

At a press conference, Downtown Seattle Association CEO Jon Scholes, who is a great guy, inaccurately said that people on the street refusing services is a myth and is not a thing.

The city's own numbers answer it. Seattle's Human Services Department recorded 7,565 shelter offers. Only 1,884 were accepted. Three out of four offers were refused.

That refusal is the disease itself. I watched it for over a decade with my sister. She held a doctorate in clinical psychology, and she still fought treatment with everything she had, because the addicted brain protects access to the drug above every other thing. She died in 2020, incapacitated, her free will gone.

Advanced addiction is a terminal illness. It remodels the brain until the person can no longer choose help. Then we point to the refusal, call it a choice, and leave them on the street to die.

People are starting to wake up to this. I wrote about my sister here:

Commish holds a 25-point lead with Pickens and Aubrey still to play, while Hamed has K9 in a revenge game against Seattle. Can Kenneth Walker put together a masterclass and make Monday interesting? Both defenses combined for a whopping zero points, but the biggest storyline was Tee Higgins showing out against his former fantasy team. Hamed traded Higgins to Commish for Waddle and McConkey just a couple weeks ago, and that performance might end up deciding this matchup.

Abhai vs Jahson

Jahson got a breakout performance from Quinshon Judkins and some production from Puka, while both defenses decided scoring points was optional this week. Abhai got 20 points from Josh Jacobs in his return and a big week from Luther Burden, but his surprise Jalen Nailor start didn’t exactly work out. It all comes down to Dak Prescott needing 28 points Monday night for Abhai to steal this one. America’s Team has one job.

Ajay vs Vik

Ajay is trying to hand the undefeated Vik his first loss, and suddenly the upset is looking very realistic. Despite a -3 from his defense and a Sam LaPorta disaster, Ajay got 27 from Drake Maye, 26 from Jamo, and 27 from McBride. Vik responded with big performances from St. Brown and Kyren, plus a solid Kamara outing. It’s 117-76, with Ajay holding Jason Myers against Mahomes and Javonte Williams. Vik entered the week undefeated, but he’s now projected to lose. Is this finally where the streak ends?

Amir vs Tanvir

Amir leads 119-89 after a ridiculous second half from Joe Burrow and Ashton Jeanty, with Zay Flowers also putting together a big performance. Unfortunately, Charlie Kirk contributed a very impressive zero points to the operation. Tanvir didn’t have one massive performance, but Caleb Williams, Harvey, Warren, and London all delivered solid outings. He’s still got JSN, Mekhi Lemon, and Kelce against Amir’s Seahawks defense. Down 30 with three players left, the rookie has a real opportunity to pull this off.

Gopi vs Shaan

Gopi’s running backs came to work today. McCaffrey and Rhamondre Stevenson both dropped 22+, and the Vikings defense might be the only defense in this entire league that remembered how fantasy scoring works. Even with Garrett Wilson and Nico Collins disappointing, Gopi has built himself a comfortable lead. Meanwhile, Shaan had a rough afternoon. Wan’Dale didn’t offer much, and Bowers couldn’t get going either. Gopi leads 87-53 with Goedert remaining, while Shaan needs Saquon, Worthy, and the Chiefs defense to get him back in business. Plenty of firepower left, but somebody needs to wake this team up.

Seeno vs Abdul

One of the closest matchups heading into tonight. Abdul holds a three-point lead after getting 23 from Geno Smith, 19 from Braylon Allen, and seeing Loveland finally come to life. Seeno got a solid game from Goff, but his running backs struggled before Tony Pollard decided to casually drop 36 points and carry the entire operation. Chase and Nabers also delivered. Now it’s Seeno’s Cowboys defense and Harrison Butker against Abdul’s CeeDee Lamb. This one could come down to the final possession Monday night.

A lot of football left, an undefeated streak on the line, and several managers about to spend the next 24 hours staring at their fantasy apps. Good luck to everyone except Hamed.

– Commish’s Office

BRANIFF HISTORY TODAY - On this day, Wednesday, October 25, 1967, Braniff International inaugurated the first nonstop service between Quito's Mariscal Sucre International Airport (original airport), Ecuador, and Miami International Airport, Florida. In the summer of 1967, Braniff began taking delivery of its new McDonnell Douglas DC-8-62 Intercontinental Jets, which were assigned for the first time to Quito schedules.

Braniff Airways had been serving Ecuador since the first day it began service between the US Mainland and Latin America on June 4, 1948. However, the company initially served Guayaquil although Quito was originally awarded to the carrier in the original route authorization from the Civil Aeronautics Board on May 22, 1946. Service to Quito did not begin until the February 1, 1967, merger with Pan American Grace Airways, which did serve the city. The merger also added Braniff service at Santiago and Antofagasta, Chile, and Cali, Colombia.

Service to Quito was operated via either the Braniff/Eastern Interchange Service or the Braniff/Pan Am/National Interchange Service to New York and Miami, respectively. Nonstop service between Quito and Miami, was initially only offered on northbound flights every Wednesday, via the Eastern Interchange, which operated over a route from Buenos Aires to Santiago, Antofagasta, and Lima, before proceeding to Quito.

The interchange flight continued nonstop to Miami and then to New York JFK, where it terminated. Quito passengers also enjoyed nonstop service to Cali on Friday and Monday; Guayaquil on Tuesday; Lima every Saturday and Thursday and Panama City/Balboa on Mondays and Sundays. The Pan Am/National Interchange Service operated over a route from Lima to Guayaquil, Quito and then proceeded to Cali; Panama City/Balboa; Miami and finally New York Kennedy on Mondays, Fridays, and Sundays.

Special inaugural ceremonies were held in Quito that were hosted by Braniff Vice President of Latin America Division Charles S. South and Staff Vice President Louis Garcia. Also attending were Braniff Regional Vice President or Country Manager Jose Salvador and District Sales Manager Miguel Burbano. Dignitaries in attendance included Ecuadorian General Jose Banderas who was the Ecuador Air Force and Minister of Defense Agustin Febres Cordero. Charles South presented the dignitaries with special inaugural mementos.

text:
Frank “Gags” Gagliano, the Hall of Fame coach who guided more than a dozen Olympians across six decades, has died. He was 89.

Gagliano coached at nearly every level of the sport. As an assistant at Manhattan College, he helped the Jaspers win the 1973 NCAA indoor team title. He spent 18 years leading Georgetown, where his teams won 23 Big East championships and produced 140 All-Americans, and he was twice named national coach of the year.

At an age when most coaches retire, he became one of the country’s top professional coaches. He led the Reebok Enclave, the Nike Farm Team, Oregon Track Club Elite and, from 2010, the New Jersey-New York Track Club. His Olympians included John Trautmann, Steve Holman, Nicole Teter, Jonathon Riley, Nick Symmonds, Christian Smith, Julie Culley and Donn Cabral. At the 2008 U.S. Olympic Trials, Symmonds and Smith were part of the famous “Oregon Sweep” of the men’s 800m at Hayward Field. 

A Bronx native, Gagliano was a quarterback at the University of Richmond, not a runner. He began coaching track in 1960 at Roselle Catholic High School in New Jersey, which had hired him with the promise of starting a football team that never came. In 1965, Roselle Catholic became the first high school to win both the DMR and 2-mile relay at the Penn Relays.

“I didn’t know anything about track,” he said in a 2014 interview. “But I accepted the offer because I really wanted to coach.”

Gags became one of the most influential coaches in American distance running. His philosophy was simple: strength plus speed. And when you hear “Hit it!” on the final turn, change gears.

Gagliano was inducted into the USTFCCCA Hall of Fame in 2003. This July, USA Track and Field named the men’s 800m at its national championships in his honor.
