text:
The Art of the Deal: Jared Kushner’s Hacked Phone Revealed His Secret Negotiations—Including More Than $700 Million in Transfers
An exclusive excerpt from ‘Princes and Thieves: Jared Kushner and Mohamed bin Zayed’s Secret Plot to Remake the Middle East’ examines how bank accounts linked the president’s son-in-law—and former senior adviser—to Israel, the UAE, and Saudi Arabia.

By Matthew Cole - 11 min. read (Vanity Fair)

In late spring 2020, a source I knew to be reliable called me with a story. The Dutch government had hacked into Jared Kushner’s phone and monitored him as he accessed a Dubai-based bank account. What was odd, the source said, was that the money in the account—hundreds of millions of dollars—had come from a bank in Azerbaijan. Most importantly, Kushner appeared to have transferred significant amounts of money from the Dubai account to other individuals, including a warlord, a mercenary and a one-time hit man. The story sounded preposterous, I told my source. And yet.

Six months later, I found myself speaking with someone else about the UAE government and their use of mercenaries in conflicts around the Middle East and Africa when I asked, on a whim, whether they knew anything about Kushner and bank transfers from a UAE account. My acquaintance grew quiet. Then they replied, “Yes.”

Over the next four years, I came to learn that, sometime in late 2017, the Netherlands Defense Intelligence and Security Service (MIVD) made a startling discovery. A General Staff of the Armed Forces of the Russian Federation (GRU) operative, a dark web hacker specializing in stolen bank data, was traveling to the UK for an espionage mission. They reached out to the British government for permission to apprehend him when he arrived. The British agreed.

When the Russian national arrived in England, the Dutch informed him that he had two options: he could work for them against the GRU, or the British would arrest him. Once in UK government custody, the operative would be charged with espionage. If convicted, he would spend years in a British prison. The Russian chose to change his employer.

Later that year, the Russian operative gave the Dutch spies access to one of the GRU’s most sensitive assets. Located in Rostov, Russia, the GRU’s hacking and cyber team operated a remote server on which they stored some of their bounty. During their search through these secret files, the Dutch found something astonishing: screenshots of Jared Kushner’s iPhone.

In The Hague, the MIVD hacking team tried to reverse engineer the Russian penetration of Kushner’s iPhone. Kushner owned what was then the latest model, the iPhone X. Released in November 2017, it featured Face ID, a state-of-the-art security feature that Apple had promoted at its launch. The Dutch team had been trying to pick the phone’s door lock, so to speak, when it occurred to them that the Russians may have found an unlocked window to gain entry instead. Their hypothesis was correct. By early 2018, the MIVD had found a vulnerability in the iPhone that gave them access. The security exploit wasn’t perfect, however. Some malware allows a hacker to turn a victim’s phone into a microphone and video camera, turn the phone on or off, and pull and add files. The Dutch solution did not provide that level of access. Instead, when Kushner used the phone, they could see his screen. Almost as soon as they got inside, the intelligence service began capturing every image of Kushner’s screen as he used it, filing their own cache of surveillance on their internal computer servers.

As they monitored Kushner’s phone, they discovered he used it to log in to a UAE bank account. By the time the Dutch spies had visibility into the phone, the account had received hundreds of millions of dollars from a bank in Azerbaijan. Their initial assessment was that the bank account was affiliated with the government there.

For the MIVD hackers, the bank account became an intelligence mystery to unravel. Nearly everything they worked on had a tinge of Russian conspiracy. A little over a year into Trump’s first presidency, the MIVD, like FBI agents and federal prosecutors in Washington working on the Robert Mueller investigation, had only part of the story.

Kushner, UAE ruler Mohamed bin Zayed (MBZ) and Mohammed bin Salman (MBS) of Saudi Arabia, converged at an auspicious moment. MBS wanted to be crown prince. MBZ wanted to blow up Obama’s Iran nuclear deal, and Kushner wanted both to help him force the Palestinians into a deal that Israel would accept. Despite the perception of his wealth, Kushner was not entirely financially independent of his parents, and the family business, Kushner Companies, faced a billion-dollar loan coming due on their trophy property, the Manhattan office building at 666 Fifth Avenue.

Early in the first Trump administration, MBZ and MBS offered to pay for a slush fund dedicated to helping the new administration with foreign policy goals. The idea was to help pay for Trump’s promised wall between Mexico and the US, for example, in an effort to secure a second term in the White House. The two Arab royals initially discussed with Kushner putting more than $10 billion into the effort. Within months, though, as MBZ pushed the Trump administration to help back MBS’s effort to become his country’s crown prince—and future king—the broader foreign policy slush fund idea fizzled. Instead, MBZ and MBS initially, and then MBZ alone, put at least $2 billion into at least two bank accounts for Kushner. It is unclear how the royals organized their $2 billion in combined payments, but they effectively split the cost. For the purposes of explanation, it is best to understand where and how each bank account was controlled.

Bank account Alpha was held at First Abu Dhabi Bank, the largest in the UAE, and was overseen by MBZ’s brother, Tahnoon bin Zayed, who served as the bank’s chairman. Beginning in 2017, the Saudis and Emiratis transferred roughly $750 million into the Alpha account. Alpha would be used as a foreign policy fund. This money would be overseen and partially managed by Kushner and MBZ, who, in their effort to strike a grand bargain to end the Israeli-Palestinian conflict, believed the region’s map needed to be redrawn.

“Jared was looking for shortcuts in his diplomacy,” a source who knew of the UAE’s deal with Kushner said. This person held discussions with both senior UAE and Israeli officials about the secret financial arrangement between Kushner, the UAE, and, at least initially, Saudi Arabia. “Jared promised MBZ that he’d push their agenda with Trump if they participated in a fund. He wanted normalization with Israel so that business could take off.” A slush fund—a shared pool of money for off-the-books diplomatic objectives—was a common form of Gulf Arab government corruption, this person explained. “The Emiratis and the Saudis do this once a year. A billion or two is nothing for them, and if it gets them what they want, it’s money well spent.”

The Alpha account looked like the funding source of a UAE government program, by which MBZ paid his bureaucrats their salaries or funded government-run schools. But how and through whom the money flowed into the Alpha account revealed that it was intended to remain secret, more akin to a covert and illicit scheme, given that it was managed in part by a senior advisor to the president of the United States.

The Dutch spies who monitored the Alpha account noted that all of it was sent by a bank in Azerbaijan in American dollars. Azerbaijan plays a unique role in money laundering. Its central bank maintains high levels of US dollars in its reserves but does not adhere to the highest standards of bank transparency. As a result, Azerbaijani banks have well-established but unadvertised practices of serving as way stations for large transfers, in which a foreign currency is exchanged for an equal amount in dollars. For a roughly 6 to 7 percent fee on the transaction, some Azerbaijani banks will accept a transfer from a client who wishes to move Saudi riyals or Emirati dirhams totaling hundreds of millions of dollars. The Saudi or Emirati client sends the money to the Azerbaijani bank, which then uses a different internal bank account to transfer the equivalent US dollars to the client’s requested destination. For auditors, this shadow trade can’t be discerned.

A shallow audit, as the Dutch tried while monitoring Kushner’s iPhone, revealed nothing more than what appeared to be an Azerbaijani government–linked bank account that sent hundreds of millions of dollars to an account in Dubai. But there was another aspect of the Alpha account that the Dutch couldn’t see or understand, one that helped reveal the secret purpose of the money. Kushner did not own the bank account at First Abu Dhabi Bank. He was a signatory for an account managed and owned by an Emirati charity.

When MBZ and MBS first began contributing to the Alpha account in 2017, the Watani Al Emarat Foundation, a UAE government-funded charity, was run by Dherar Belhoul Al Falasi. Al Falasi was a technocrat and a member of the Federal National Council, and friends with one of MBZ’s closest friends and advisors. As a result, Al Falasi and the Watani Foundation had a second mission. The charity was used as a cover to move money in support of the country’s secret military and intelligence operations overseas. Under the Watani cover, Al Falasi helped facilitate the UAE’s secret weapons-purchasing programs, one confidential source who had direct knowledge of the charity’s proliferation program revealed. This source said that the Emiratis believed that the program’s status as a charity made its international transactions less likely to be scrutinized and therefore served as a useful cover for funding MBZ and his brother’s secret wars.

MBZ and Tahnoon made Kushner a signatory on the Alpha account with Watani. As a signatory, Jared had access to it and could, in theory, make transactions, but it technically wasn’t his account. One way to view what Kushner did with the Alpha account is to imagine him as the director of the CIA. Had he been running the government entity that managed and ran secret foreign programs, maintaining the account, again, with presidential approval and congressional disclosure, Kushner’s conduct would have been within his job’s responsibilities. But he was not the director of the CIA, whose position is approved by the Senate and whose operations are overseen and accountable to Congress. Instead, Kushner was overseen only by his father-in-law, who, according to four senior Trump administration officials—two national security advisors, a White House chief of staff, and a former CIA director—were unaware of any presidential authorization for Kushner to access a foreign government bank account. (Kushner’s counsel, however, said Kushner did not make any agreements or arrangements with leaders or officials in foreign countries that were not agreed to by the President of the United States and in the best interests of the United States.)

Regardless of whether he was a signatory or the owner, Jared was required by federal government regulations and the Internal Revenue Service to disclose his access to the account. Unless disclosed to and approved by the US government and reported on his tax returns, Kushner’s access to the Alpha account may have violated US law. (A lawyer for Mr. Kushner denied that his client had any knowledge of or connection to Al Falasi, the Watani charity, or a UAE bank account and stated that he had complied with all legal requirements when dealing with foreign governments.)

In addition to the Alpha bank account, MBZ put money into at least one other account intended for Kushner. By the spring of 2018, the crown prince had moved roughly $1 billion to Israel via Azerbaijan for Kushner. We will refer to this account as the Beta bank account. It is unclear how Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu first learned of MBZ’s money for Kushner, but a person briefed on the Beta account told me that the prime minister encouraged Kushner to have the money deposited in the Israeli Central Bank, in what would appear to be a government account. It is also unclear how Kushner used the money the UAE deposited into the Beta account for him, but according to the person with knowledge of the money, its allocation was for Kushner’s personal benefit. But as with the Alpha account, there were clues in the way the Beta account was managed.

Israel’s Central Bank does not operate personal accounts. The bank holds and transfers only government funds. The government accounts use a dual-key system, which requires two authorized individuals to make any transfers from the account as an oversight mechanism. Netanyahu required Kushner to inform him before making any transactions from the Beta account.

To do so, Kushner passed his messages through Ambassador David M. Friedman, who frequently met with Netanyahu. With the money in the Central Bank, it would be difficult, if not impossible, to connect MBZ’s payment to Jared. It is unclear if spies in the Netherlands had any indication of the Beta account. (Ambassador Friedman denied that he had any knowledge of, or involvement with, any UAE money made available to Kushner, or that he passed messages on Kushner’s behalf. “I know absolutely nothing about any of these allegations,” Friedman said, “and the specific allegations about me or my alleged involvement in this alleged scheme are 100% false.” Kushner’s counsel also said Kushner “has no idea” about any such account, and insisted that “there are no accounts and never were.”)

Apparently, Kushner faced the challenge of moving money from the Beta account in Israel to other accounts where he could have untraceable access to the funds. One person who worked with Kushner to move the money out of Israel said that much of it went to bank accounts in Cyprus before being moved elsewhere.

During Kushner’s secret financial arrangement with MBZ, he helped negotiate a third, altogether distinct account. As part of what was, at the time, a secret warming of diplomatic relations between Israel and the UAE, Kushner helped negotiate an agreement by Israel to help defend the UAE from a major Iranian military attack. The UAE needed to cover the cost of the emergency defense, however, and the government secretly made another transfer to Israel’s Central Bank. This was something like a rainy-day defense fund. Combined, the three accounts represented a secret foreign policy negotiated by Kushner with the leaders of Israel, the UAE and Saudi Arabia.

Although Kushner’s position as senior advisor to the president was unpaid, he was an official government employee. Not only did his position require financial disclosures for ethics regulations, but each year he worked in the White House, he had to file both a public and confidential financial form, known as the Executive Branch Personnel Public Financial Disclosure Report, also known as a 278e disclosure. Because he had access to classified government secrets, Kushner was required to disclose any bank account to which he had signatory—or beneficiary—access.

Kushner’s apparent betrayal of the public trust, however, went further than his failure to disclose the secret Alpha account in the UAE or the Beta account in Israel. By giving him access to roughly $2 billion, regardless of how the money was used, MBZ and MBS were paying for his influence within the US government. Any efforts he made to shape US policy that came from a foreign government that had provided him with money would make him an agent of a foreign power. US law requires citizens who lobby on behalf of a foreign power to declare themselves and the country they are working on behalf of to the Justice Department.

One former prosecutor who worked on the Mueller investigation said that if Kushner promised anything to MBZ and MBS in return for the money they offered him—even if it was just speaking to his father-in-law—he may have violated federal bribery laws, as well as the foreign agent statute. (Mr. Kushner’s lawyer denied that Kushner violated any laws while serving in the White House.)

I write to you from the cold, glowing trenches of the Operations Center, my knuckles weary from the unending cadence of keypresses. The front lines are in total disarray. A dark day has fallen upon the territory: a great vulnpocalypse has breached our defenses, and the enemy marches through unpatched zero-days with relentless malice.

Earlier this morning, Captain Harrison received word that the perimeter firewall had collapsed. A foul exploit, disguised as a harmless web request, swept through our flanks. Before our brigade could deploy the emergency patches, half our domain controllers were captured, their secrets locked behind a cruel ransom note.

The battle rages on multiple fronts. Corporal Jenkins fought valiantly to revoke elevated privileges before he was isolated by a sea of phishing emails, while young Private Miller spent three grueling hours attempting to restore the active directory from a tape backup that was, alas, corrupted six moons ago.

We are low on provisions. The coffee rations have been depleted since mid-day, and the incident response playbook offers little solace against the tide of incoming alerts. Yet, we hold the line. We have severed the external VPN, fortified our remaining subnets with local firewalls, and declared a state of zero trust across the camp.

If the server racks hold through the night, we may yet push back the threat actors and compile a post-mortem report before Sunday break. Give my fondest regards to the neighborhood. Tell them that though the packets fall heavy around us, your son remains uncompromised.

Your faithful servant,

- Captain Tib3rius

text:
As for your second post, these are not actual contradictions either. Like the earlier examples, they are apparent issues that resolve with careful attention to context, grammar, and what the text actually claims.
Human Sacrifice: Leviticus 18:21 vs. Judges 11:30–31
Leviticus 18:21 (along with Leviticus 20:2–5, Deuteronomy 12:31, and 18:10) clearly and repeatedly forbids child sacrifice as an abomination to the Lord. The question is whether Judges 11 presents God commanding, approving, or accepting Jephthah’s action.
It does not. The narrative records Jephthah’s rash vow and its outcome during the period of the judges, when “everyone did what was right in his own eyes” (Judges 21:25). Two main interpretations exist among scholars and readers:
•  Literal sacrifice view: Jephthah did kill his daughter as a burnt offering. This is a tragic, sinful act of a flawed human being. The Bible frequently records people’s failures and sins without endorsing them (compare David’s actions or the broader cycles of disobedience in Judges). God never commanded or approved it. Jephthah is later mentioned in Hebrews 11 for his faith in the battle, not for the vow.
•  Dedication view: He fulfilled the vow by dedicating her to lifelong service to the Lord (resulting in permanent virginity). Support for this includes the daughter mourning her virginity rather than her impending death (Judges 11:37), the emphasis that “she knew no man” (11:39), the absence of any description of an altar, blood, or killing, and the fact that the Hebrew of the vow can be read disjunctively (“shall surely be the Lord’s, or I will offer it up as a burnt offering”). This aligns with the law’s prohibition.
In either reading, there is no contradiction with the clear prohibition of human sacrifice, because the text does not present the outcome as God’s will or an approved act of worship. ￼
Power of God: Matthew 19:26 vs. Judges 1:19
Matthew 19:26 (“With God all things are possible”) affirms God’s absolute omnipotence. Judges 1:19 does not claim that God was unable to do something.
The verse says: “The Lord was with Judah, and he took possession of the hill country, but he could not drive out the inhabitants of the plain because they had chariots of iron.” The subject of “could not” is Judah (or the men of Judah), not God. Modern translations make this clearer (e.g., NIV: “The Lord was with the men of Judah. They took possession of the hill country, but they were unable to drive the people from the plains…”). ￼
God’s presence with His people does not mean every battle is automatically won regardless of faith, obedience, or fear. The broader context of Judges shows incomplete conquest tied to Israel’s compromises (see Judges 2:1–3). Later in the same book (Judges 4), God decisively defeats an army with 900 iron chariots. The point of Judges 1:19 is Judah’s limited success due to the practical and spiritual challenges they faced, not a limitation on God’s power.

These examples follow the same pattern as the previous ones: the apparent conflicts disappear when the full context, the precise wording, and the distinction between what God commands versus what humans do (or fail to do) are taken into account.

text:
The more I look into @RaidLords, the more I realize that choosing a Champion could be one of the most important decisions in the game. ⚔️

Every player has a different approach to combat. Some prefer overwhelming their enemies with raw damage, while others focus on defense, control, and supporting their army when battles get difficult.

Personally, I think the real challenge is finding the right balance. A Berserker might be deadly on the offensive, but a Guardian who can withstand heavy attacks could be the key to surviving a difficult raid. Meanwhile, a Warlord might offer a completely different way to approach the battlefield.

What interests me most is the progression system. Building a Champion shouldn’t just be about collecting powerful equipment. It should be about developing a playstyle, making smart decisions, and gradually turning your knight into a force to be reckoned with.

The Champion Trials also sound like an exciting challenge. Fighting bandit knights alone is a great opportunity to see whether your build actually works or needs improvement.

I’m curious to see how much strategy goes into mastering each path once the battles get more competitive.

If you were starting your journey in RaidLords today, which Champion would you choose: Guardian, Warlord, or Berserker? 👀

text:
Rocky Marciano TKO's former Heavyweight Champion Joe Louis in the 8th round, on October 26, 1951, at Madison Square Garden.

Marciano is one of the three (Undisputed) World Heavyweight Champions (the other are Lennox Lewis and Ingemar Johansson) to have beaten every fighter they've ever faced in the professional ring and the only one to permanently retire undefeated.
----------------------------------------------------------
From The Fight City (written by Michael Carbert on Marciano's birthday in 2022 - Marciano would have been 100 in September of 2023):

What makes Rocky Marciano special? Well, for starters there’s the fact he began boxing seriously at the ripe old age of 23, turning pro at 25. For someone to take up the sport that late and go on to stunning success is unheard of. Rocky did learn some of the rudiments of fisticuffs as a youngster, and while stationed with the army in Europe he sparred regularly, but he really only began boxing with serious intent after his attempts to make it as a baseball player hit a dead end. Not often (as in, never) does someone in their twenties turn to prizefighting as “Plan B” and go on to be a world champion. Crazy.
Then there’s the fact that, even back in the day, Rocky was a tad small for a heavyweight, but despite this he established himself as a certified wrecking machine. Standing 5’10” and rarely weighing more than 188 pounds, and in a time before anyone started taking steroids, Marciano had to focus on being in nothing less than phenomenal condition to overcome disadvantages in size and weight. For example, when Marciano knocked out Joe Louis in 1951, the aging former champion was almost thirty pounds heavier. But as they say, power is the great equalizer, and despite his small stature, Marciano could lower the boom like few fighters in boxing history. He blasted Louis out of the ring and then went on to achieve an amazing 88% knockout ratio before all was said and done.
Admittedly, Rocky competed in a rather depleted heavyweight division, but he ducked no one and, thanks to his power, ferocity and amazing stamina, he holds wins over such certified legends as Louis, Jersey Joe Walcott, Ezzard Charles and Archie Moore. His ring style necessitated taking shots, but he had a chin of granite and was down only twice, to Walcott and KO king Moore. He faced the best fighters of his time and stopped them all inside the distance; his one-punch pasting of Walcott for the title is one of the greatest, not to mention one of the most brutal, knockouts in boxing history. He featured in three contests hailed by Ring magazine as Fight Of The Year, and his reputation as a relentless, all-action punching machine made him a hot ticket; huge crowds came to all of his title fights. But then, suddenly, it was over.
Few expected Marciano to end his career when he did. He was a dominant champion, hugely successful, only 32-years-old, but his family wanted him to walk away from the fight game. Even so, following his final match, a knockout over Moore in September of 1955, he told the press, “Personally, at this point, I don’t feel I should retire.”
At the time no one was particularly vexed about Rocky’s undefeated record one way or the other. Sure it was an impressive run, but back then defeats were not viewed as the terrible disgrace they are today. Losses were part of the game. Marciano’s spotless win streak was regarded as something weird and freakish as much as it was seen as a testament to his pugilistic greatness. More to the point, at the time few, if any, historians and boxing scribes saw Rocky as the “TBE” of the heavyweight division. Pretty much everyone rated Louis, Jack Dempsey, James J. Jeffries and Jack Johnson as superior, and all of those fighters had tasted defeat. Marciano’s image as an all-time great was something which gained credence more in hindsight, his stature rising on a tide of nostalgia in the 1960s and 70s.
Today it’s difficult to determine his standing when the heavyweight division has become the domain of guys who belong at the top of a beanstalk. A fight between a 188 pound Marciano and a 250 pound Lennox Lewis, for example, is a non-starter for obvious reasons. And yet, a list of history’s greatest heavyweight champions that doesn’t include the name ‘Rocky Marciano’ is generally viewed as misguided. His power, strength, toughness and will-to-win, plus his victories over some truly great names, guarantee him pugilistic immortality.
But as for 49-0 …
The whole truth did not come out for years, but when Marciano retired from boxing in April of 1956 his decision was less about the wishes of his family and more about the fact that Rocky was fed up with his manager, Al Weill. A former professional ballroom dancer, Weill was a total control freak and not much fun to work with. Not only did he get a fifty percent take of Marciano’s ring earnings, but he insisted on restricting Rocky’s public appearances and demanded a percentage of any payments the champion received for work outside the ring. If Marciano did a commercial or a television appearance, or even just a talk at the local boat show, Weill got a big, juicy bite of the proceeds.
The result was Rocky became paranoid about any and all financial transactions and did everything he could to conceal his income from Weill. This led to some bizarre behavior. His daughter has recounted inadvertently discovering thousands of dollars in a paper bag Rocky had forgotten under his chair in a movie theater, and it’s well known that he hid cash in all kinds of strange places, including light fixtures and curtain rods. He happily turned away checks worth thousands in favor of only hundreds in cash, because there was always a chance checks could be tracked down by Weill. This obsession with money led directly to Rocky’s death when he was only 45. Offered a free flight from Chicago to Des Moines on a small private plane, he couldn’t resist. The pilot was inexperienced and the plane crashed, killing all on board.
The point is, money and Marciano’s hatred of Weill were the chief reasons for his choosing to retire when he did. His undefeated record was barely an afterthought. At the time, no one, including Rocky, really cared all that much about 49-0. Yes, becoming world champion and then retiring undefeated is an impressive accomplishment, but that by itself does not signify ring greatness and everyone at the time understood that. Besides, it was well known many of Rocky’s wins were over sub-par opponents and that at least two of his victories were suspect. The decision in the first of two matches with Ted Lowry was booed by the crowd and widely viewed as a gift, and many regarded his first points win over Roland LaStarza as a blatant robbery. But as time went on these facts faded away while the 49-0 mark accrued greater significance with the public.
Marciano had become a full-fledged legend by the 1980’s with the Rocky Balboa movies augmenting his fame (“Ya kinda remind me of ‘The Rock'”), and in 1985 Larry Holmes was in position to tie the 49-0 mark with a victory over light heavyweight champion Michael Spinks. But it was Spinks who scored a massive upset with a close decision win and Larry then went on to utter his infamous “Rocky couldn’t carry my jockstrap” line during a truly extraordinary post-fight press conference. Since then no heavyweight champion has managed to match or break the record. But even so, Marciano is hardly alone in terms of retiring undefeated, and in fact there are a number of longer and more significant win streaks.
Let’s start with Jimmy Wilde, without question one of the greatest fighters of all-time, who owns what may be the longest such streak in pugilistic history. In fact, it’s so long that it remains beyond precise account as some sources say Wilde went 93-0 before losing to Tancy Lee in 1915, while others say the number went as high as 104. Either way, it’s a mark that dwarfs 50-0. Wilde is regarded by many as both the greatest flyweight of all-time and the best fighter to ever emerge from Great Britain, and in addition to retiring with an incredible final tally of 132-3-1, he had 99 knockouts in his 132 wins, making him, pound-for-pound, one of the greatest punchers in boxing history. Bottom line: if Jimmy Wilde doesn’t put 49-0 into perspective for you, then you need to put down the “TBE” Kool-Aid and give your head a shake.
But check this out: Young Griffo won 124 fights in a row, while the great Packy McFarland won 98. Sugar Ray Robinson went 91 straight without a loss, while Willie Pep owns not one, but two amazing win streaks. The “Will o’ the Wisp” reeled off 62 victories before dropping a decision to Sammy Angott, and then picked up where he left off to notch 72 in a row. Julio Cesar Chavez vanquished 87 consecutive opponents, while Carlos Monzon once went eighty straight without a loss. And though the records are a bit sketchy, some maintain that British lightweight Hal Bagwell won a grand total of 180 consecutive pro tilts, but you don’t hear anyone saying Bagwell is the “TBE,” do you?
But we’re far from done. Ruben Olivares boasts 61 consecutive victories; Freddie Steele put together 54, and Carlos Zarate, 52. Nino Benvenuti had a run of 65 straight, while the amazing Harry Greb once racked up over seventy wins without a loss in less than three years. Duilio Loi put together a run of 59 fights without a defeat, while minimum-weight champion Chayaphon Moonsri went 54-0 before taking his first loss. Then there’s Ricardo Lopez retiring with a record of 51-0-1, while Jimmy Barry, aka “The Little Tiger,” walked away with a record of 58-0. And don’t forget lesser known middleweight contender Teddy Yarosz who went 58-0, in the process beating guys like Billy Conn, Lou Brouillard, Vince Dundee, Eddie “Babe” Risko and Archie Moore. But no one goes around saying Teddy Yarosz is the best ever; maybe they should.
Perhaps Larry Merchant put it best when he stated that Marciano’s famous win streak “doesn’t make him a greater fighter, but a larger figure.” In other words, it’s a notable and famous achievement, but it does not constitute iron-clad evidence of Marciano’s greatness. And the same is true for Floyd Mayweather, whose 50-0 mark means very little in the context of boxing history. Especially when win number fifty came against a guy with a sterling ring record of 0-0-0.
Of course the Mayweather vs McGregor fight of 2017 should never have been sanctioned and should not count as an official bout on Floyd’s pro record. 
But on the other hand, nothing could be more fitting that such an absurd swindle, a con which fleeced the public of hundreds of millions of dollars, should be the one that broke the hallowed 49-0 mark. 
For years, Floyd has been much more about the sizzle, not the steak, and Mayweather’s 50-0 ledger will always be more about marketing than anything else. Just as the aptly titled “Money Fight” had little to do with sports and everything to do with exploiting boxing so Floyd and Conor McGregor could collect outlandish paydays.
Simply put, “The Rock’s” 49-0 will always mean more than Floyd’s 50-0. 
In his final fight, Marciano took on a Hall of Fame champion and true all-time great in Archie Moore, surviving a knockdown to go toe-to-toe with the man with the most elite-level knockouts in boxing history, before stopping him in nine thrilling rounds. 
Meanwhile, Floyd took on an MMA fighter with almost no boxing experience, carried him for several rounds, and then beat him up when he got tired.
Floyd Mayweather added nothing to his legacy with that win, quite the opposite. And in fact, his credentials as a true all-time great were shaky to begin with. When boxing historian Monte Cox compiled his lists of the all-time greatest boxers, Floyd’s name failed to make an appearance. Here’s Mr. Cox explaining why:
“Floyd Mayweather’s career does not give him a spot [in the top ten welterweights of all-time]. Luis Rodriguez, for example, had a better career than Floyd [with wins over] Emile Griffith, Benny Paret, Hurricane Carter, Curtis Cokes, Georgie Benton and Bennie Briscoe. I cannot in all honesty put Mayweather in the top ten welterweights based on a career of hand-picked opponents and having never unified a major title. Floyd avoided fights with Mosley, Margarito and Pacquiao when they meant something. Mayweather just does not have the competition to be considered an all-time great.”
So Happy Birthday, Rocky, and rest easy. I doubt 49-0 ever meant half as much to you as it does to many Floyd Mayweather fans, but, surprisingly, it still means more than 50-0. And that’s the truth.

Canton Weekly Update | October 19 to 25

1. Universal Burn was approved for @CantonNetwork. The plan would make production transactions on businesses’ dedicated Canton systems pay fees that burn $CC. 

2. @temple_ny chose @tZERO to support a tokenized securities platform on Canton. It also launched Cash RFQ, letting institutions compare trade prices from multiple firms. 

3. @circle and @SPGlobal were among 40 approved Canton validator applications. MainNet onboarding is a separate step. 

4. @progmat_en shared findings from its 69 organisation study into tokenized Japanese government bonds. The group is targeting November for Canton trials using test versions of bonds, deposits and stablecoins, once preparations are ready.

5. @trize_io integrated @chainlink CCIP, allowing tokenized assets to move in both directions between Canton and supported Ethereum compatible networks.

6. Canton’s Super Validators approved a plan to enforce existing CC locking commitments for Featured Apps and Super Validators automatically on the network. The rollout will happen in stages.

7. $NEOPRIME, developed with @hectoinc, is now trading on @Cantex_io. The token offers exposure to pre IPO companies, targeting defence, space and robotics. @NeoprimeCapital’s first investment is Erebor Bank.

8. @BitSafe_Finance launched BETH, a token representing Ether on Canton. Trading against USDCx is live on @temple_ny, with wallet support added by @canton_loop.

9. @mystic_finance received funding approval for up to 2 million CC to develop shared rules for vault deposits, shares and withdrawals. @IntellectEU and @DigitalAsset’s 4 million CC project to record Super Validator reward allocations on the Canton ledger also passed funding review. Both awards depend on milestones.

10. @edeldotfinance passed $10 million in trading volume across Edel Stocks. Its Canton tokens give exposure to stocks and funds, including products linked to the S&P 500 and Nasdaq 100.

11. @KaikoData joined the UK’s wholesale tokenization taskforce. Its work will focus on market data, pricing and trading in tokenized financial markets.

12. @CantonFdn announced cooperation with Taiwanese financial and technology bodies. The work focuses on training students and financial institutions, with plans to connect tokenized Taiwanese assets to global markets.

13. @texture_capital and @obsidian_llc announced plans for @tradecraftfi’s Tradecraft ATS, a Canton venue for tokenized securities. It would settle trades using USDCx and has not launched yet.

14. @Greywick_hq is targeting launch around November 1 for cLTC, a Litecoin backed token on Canton. Its Featured Asset application is pending. An independent security audit of the full cLTC app is still planned.

15. @CantonFdn’s Tokenomics Committee approved updated Featured App reward guidance, including checks against artificial activity. Some changes still need further governance votes and implementation.

16. @CantonFdn announced plans to elect two new Board seats this year. Its framework allows up to 25 seats across five stakeholder groups, with four year terms.

17. @grofty_labs added @Cantex_io’s Cantex Connect swaps inside Grofty DEX. Users trade from Grofty Wallet and receive the tokens directly in their wallet.

18. @Kora_Protocol added a cETH and USDCx trading pair on Kora v2. cETH represents Ether on Canton.

Rarelist is designed around one core idea: genuine contributions to early Web3 projects should produce measurable upside instead of just likes. Here are the main practical benefits currently offered:

RARS points as a contribution score: Create relevant content on X and complete campaign tasks → earn RARS. These points determine your rank on project and platform leaderboards and are intended to convert into the $RARE token later (conversion details and timing still pending).
Direct monetary rewards: Season 1 has a $50,000 prize pool. Individual partner campaigns also distribute USDT, with examples including Project Sphere ($2,000), Fomopoly ($2,000 + $DEAL airdrop), and Agent Dojo (~$1,500). Rewards are competitive and based on rank.

Access and allocation perks: Higher placement can unlock whitelist spots, free mint allocations, airdrops, and other campaign-specific benefits from the projects themselves.
Priority launch access: Building a track record of contributions moves you into higher participation tiers, which the platform positions as giving priority access to curated launches and future opportunities.

Early discovery edge: Projects are curated rather than open to anyone. Creators can research and support earlier-stage teams (including via an Alpha Zone for higher-risk campaigns) before broader awareness.

Quality-over-volume design: The system detects posts automatically and has been updated to filter low-effort or spam content more aggressively. Consistent, useful content is what moves rankings rather than pure posting volume.

Low initial friction: Connect your X account to start; no wallet or deposit is required to participate and earn RARS.

Caveats worth noting: Rewards are competitive and not guaranteed. Conversion of RARS to $RARE is still prospective. The platform is early (launched Season 1 in early October 2026), so mechanics, scoring, and campaign quality are still evolving. Always review each campaign’s specific terms.

This model tries to align three groups: projects get targeted exposure, creators get compensated for research and content, and early supporters can build a visible track record that unlocks access. Whether it scales depends on execution and the quality of the projects that join.

text:
Forensically who has better positioning for a moon to earth base, considering geographical landscaping and historical logistics in this?

ChatGPT:

The United States has the strongest overall position for a sustained Moon–Earth base system. China is its strongest competitor. France, through French Guiana, has an exceptional geographic advantage for Earth-side launches.

That is my assessment from demonstrated operations and geography—not a claim that any country has already established a functioning lunar base.

1. United States: strongest combined position

Its strongest advantage is accumulated logistics: six successful Apollo landings, human surface operations, lunar ascent, orbital rendezvous, and safe return. That establishes experience across the entire transport chain, although Apollo hardware does not constitute a ready-made modern supply system. 

Florida provides an established launch complex at Kennedy/Cape Canaveral. The United States also operates deep-space communications facilities in California, Spain, and Australia, spaced around Earth to maintain contact as the planet rotates. That distributed geography matters more for sustained lunar operations than having one particularly favorable launch location. 

2. China: strongest competing integrated system

China has demonstrated a particularly relevant robotic supply-chain sequence: launch from Wenchang, far-side landing, sample collection, lunar ascent, orbital docking, and return to Inner Mongolia. Chang’e-6 completed that sequence in 2024, using the Queqiao-2 relay for communications. These are concrete building blocks for an automated lunar logistics system. 

Its proposed International Lunar Research Station targets the lunar south pole. The distinction is that its successful robotic missions are demonstrated capability; the station remains a development objective. 

3. France: especially favorable launch geography

Kourou, in French Guiana, lies about five degrees north of the equator and offers broad launch directions over the Atlantic. ESA identifies its low latitude, sparse surrounding population, and low cyclone risk as advantages. France therefore deserves consideration when the question emphasizes physical geography. However, equatorial advantages are mission-dependent; they do not automatically make Kourou the best departure point for every lunar trajectory. 

The lunar landscape changes the calculation.

A useful base needs accessible landing terrain, dependable power, manageable travel routes, communications, and proximity to usable resources. At the south pole, elevated terrain can receive extended sunlight, while shadowed craters offer potential ice resources. But mountains and crater rims can obstruct both travel and Earth communications. The best habitat location may therefore be separated from the best resource-extraction location. 

My ranking: United States for the complete operating system; China as the strongest challenger; France for a particularly advantageous Earth launch location. No country’s terrestrial location alone gives it a permanent direct corridor to a lunar base.

text:
🇺🇸 Trump Designates Chiricahua as America's 64th National Park in Arizona

🌳 America's Newest National Park: President Donald Trump signed the Chiricahua National Park Act, officially transforming Arizona's Chiricahua National Monument into the nation's 64th national park. It is the first addition to the country's national parks in six years.

🏞️ Arizona's Fourth National Park: Located in Cochise County in southeastern Arizona, Chiricahua joins Grand Canyon, Saguaro and Petrified Forest national parks. The approximately 12,000 acre landscape has been federally protected since 1924.

🌋 Extraordinary Geological Formations: Nicknamed the "Wonderland of Rocks," the park features towering volcanic stone pillars, balanced boulders and dramatic rock formations created by volcanic activity approximately 27 million years ago.

🦅 Wildlife and Natural Conservation: The park protects a distinctive Sky Island ecosystem where deserts, grasslands and forests converge. It provides habitat for diverse wildlife and offers opportunities for hiking, birdwatching, camping and stargazing.

🏛️ Historic Bipartisan Achievement: The designation followed years of bipartisan congressional efforts, including legislation sponsored by Republican Representative Juan Ciscomani and Democratic Representative Greg Stanton. The park also preserves significant Chiricahua Apache cultural heritage.

💰 Economic Opportunities for Arizona: State and local officials anticipate increased tourism, hotel bookings, restaurant spending and business investment in nearby communities, particularly Willcox and Cochise County.

🚶 What Changes for Visitors: The new designation does not expand the park's boundaries or automatically increase its funding. Existing hiking trails, scenic drives and camping opportunities remain available, while conservation advocates emphasize the importance of sufficient staffing and maintenance resources.

🇺🇸 A Milestone in American Conservation: Chiricahua's elevation recognizes more than a century of federal protection while bringing greater national attention to one of the Southwest's distinctive natural and cultural landscapes.

News via Mercedes-AMG Petronas Formula One

Kimi Antonelli won Sunday’s Italian Grand Prix with team-mate George Russell P2.

It was a thrilling drive from Kimi as he charged through the field from P19 to become the first Italian to win their home race since Ludovico Scarfiotti in 1966.

It also marks Mercedes 250th Grand Prix victory as a power unit manufacturer and the marque’s eighth victory at Monza; it’s first since 2018 at the ‘Temple of Speed’.

Starting out of position, Kimi started on the Hard tyre but was able to change to the Medium compound under an early race red flag. By that point, he had already gained seven places to run P12.

George meanwhile ran the conventional one-stop from P2 by starting on the Medium and taking the Hard under the red flag, with the clear goal to run to the end on that tyre as he led.

Kimi’s progressed continued once the race restarted and cycled through to battle his team-mate for the lead.

A mid-race Virtual Safety Car gave the team the option of pitting Kimi for a new Medium tyre, with signs suggesting that his original Medium tyre wouldn’t have the life to get to the end of the race.

He rejoined in P6 but made short work of cars ahead; in the final stages he closed the gap to George before making the pass for the lead with three laps left.

Our duo took the flag comfortably ahead of the rest of the field to secure the win, and the 50th for an Italian in F1.

Deputy Technical Director Simone Resta represented the team on the podium at his home race.

The team now leads the Constructors’ Championship by 122 points with Kimi heading the Drivers’ standings by 66 points from his team-mate George.

The Italian Grand Prix (Italian: Gran Premio d'Italia) is the fifth oldest national motor racing Grand Prix (after the French Grand Prix, the United States Grand Prix, the Spanish Grand Prix and the Russian Grand Prix), having been held since 1921. Since 2013, the Grand Prix has been held the most times, with 97 editions as of 2026.

It is one of the two Grands Prix (along with the British) which has run every season as an event of the Formula One World Championship Grands Prix, continuously since the championship was introduced in 1950.

Every Formula One Italian Grand Prix in the World Championship era has been held at Monza except in 1980, when it was held at Imola.

Mercedes-Benz, a German automotive brand of the Mercedes-Benz Group, has been involved in Formula One as both team owner and engine manufacturer for various periods since 1954. The current Mercedes-Benz Grand Prix Limited, competing as Mercedes-AMG Petronas Formula One Team, is based in Brackley, England, and holds a German racing licence. An announcement was made in December 2020 that Ineos planned to take a one third equal ownership stake alongside the Mercedes-Benz Group and Toto Wolff; this came into effect on 25 January 2022. Mercedes-branded teams are often referred to by the nickname, the "Silver Arrows" (German: Silberpfeile).

What makes the Austrian Grand Prix special – and why you should see it

Discover what makes the F1 weekend in Austria unmissable.

The Austrian Grand Prix is a classic, and might just be held at one of the most picturesque track on the F1 calendar. Set in the Styrian hills, around 700m above sea level, the short track features rapid lap times and plenty of overtaking opportunities.

Despite the Red Bull Ring having the fewest corners of any circuit on the schedule, it's seen many unforgettable moments throughout the years – and, as the name might suggest, is the track that Red Bull calls home.

Let's take a look at just some of the reasons why Austria is so alluring.

Austrian racing heritage

Austria, despite it's relatively small population, has heaps of racing heritage. Triple World Champion Niki Lauda was born in Vienna, winning titles for Ferrari and McLaren, and was a major factor behind Mercedes’ success while helping convince Lewis Hamilton to join the outfit in 2013.

Jochen Rindt was Austria's first champion – the only posthumous F1 title winner, having tragically passed away during his dominant 1970 season. Gerhard Berger, while never taking the title himself, scored 10 wins during his illustrious career.

More recently, the late Austrian entrepreneur Dietrich Mateschitz and former Austrian F1 racer Helmut Marko – in his role as motorsport advisor – played key roles in Red Bull's success, with the team clinching eight Drivers’ and six Constructors’ titles.

When is the 2026 Austrian Grand Prix?

The 2026 Austrian Grand Prix weekend begins on Friday 26 June, with F1 cars hitting the track for the first two Free Practice sessions, before Free Practice 3 and Qualifying take place on Saturday 27 June. The Grand Prix itself is on Sunday 28 June, at 1500 local time.

Kimi Antonelli produced a breathtaking performance, after starting the race from P19, to overtake the rest of the pack and clinch the Italian Grand Prix victory in magnificent fashion on Sunday. This is how he did it! (Credit: Formula One)

News via Mercedes-AMG Petronas Formula One
Kimi Antonelli won Sunday’s Italian Grand Prix with team-mate George Russell P2.

It was a thrilling drive from Kimi as he charged through the field from P19 to become the first Italian to win their home race since Ludovico Scarfiotti in 1966.

It also marks Mercedes 250th Grand Prix victory as a power unit manufacturer and the marque’s eighth victory at Monza; it’s first since 2018 at the ‘Temple of Speed’.

Starting out of position, Kimi started on the Hard tyre but was able to change to the Medium compound under an early race red flag. By that point, he had already gained seven places to run P12.

George meanwhile ran the conventional one-stop from P2 by starting on the Medium and taking the Hard under the red flag, with the clear goal to run to the end on that tyre as he led.

Kimi’s progressed continued once the race restarted and cycled through to battle his team-mate for the lead.

A mid-race Virtual Safety Car gave the team the option of pitting Kimi for a new Medium tyre, with signs suggesting that his original Medium tyre wouldn’t have the life to get to the end of the race.

He rejoined in P6 but made short work of cars ahead; in the final stages he closed the gap to George before making the pass for the lead with three laps left.

Our duo took the flag comfortably ahead of the rest of the field to secure the win, and the 50th for an Italian in F1.

Deputy Technical Director Simone Resta represented the team on the podium at his home race.

The team now leads the Constructors’ Championship by 122 points with Kimi heading the Drivers’ standings by 66 points from his team-mate George.

Profile

The Italian Grand Prix (Italian: Gran Premio d'Italia) is the fifth oldest national motor racing Grand Prix (after the French Grand Prix, the United States Grand Prix, the Spanish Grand Prix and the Russian Grand Prix), having been held since 1921. Since 2013, the Grand Prix has been held the most times, with 97 editions as of 2026.
It is one of the two Grands Prix (along with the British) which has run every season as an event of the Formula One World Championship Grands Prix, continuously since the championship was introduced in 1950.

Every Formula One Italian Grand Prix in the World Championship era has been held at Monza except in 1980, when it was held at Imola.

Profile

Mercedes-AMG Petronas Formula One Team
Mercedes-Benz, a German automotive brand of the Mercedes-Benz Group, has been involved in Formula One as both team owner and engine manufacturer for various periods since 1954. The current Mercedes-Benz Grand Prix Limited, competing as Mercedes-AMG Petronas Formula One Team, is based in Brackley, England, and holds a German racing licence. An announcement was made in December 2020 that Ineos planned to take a one third equal ownership stake alongside the Mercedes-Benz Group and Toto Wolff; this came into effect on 25 January 2022. Mercedes-branded teams are often referred to by the nickname, the "Silver Arrows" (German: Silberpfeile).

News via Mercedes-AMG Petronas Formula One

Kimi Antonelli won Sunday’s Italian Grand Prix with team-mate George Russell P2.

It was a thrilling drive from Kimi as he charged through the field from P19 to become the first Italian to win their home race since Ludovico Scarfiotti in 1966.

It also marks Mercedes 250th Grand Prix victory as a power unit manufacturer and the marque’s eighth victory at Monza; it’s first since 2018 at the ‘Temple of Speed’.

Starting out of position, Kimi started on the Hard tyre but was able to change to the Medium compound under an early race red flag. By that point, he had already gained seven places to run P12.

George meanwhile ran the conventional one-stop from P2 by starting on the Medium and taking the Hard under the red flag, with the clear goal to run to the end on that tyre as he led.

Kimi’s progressed continued once the race restarted and cycled through to battle his team-mate for the lead.

A mid-race Virtual Safety Car gave the team the option of pitting Kimi for a new Medium tyre, with signs suggesting that his original Medium tyre wouldn’t have the life to get to the end of the race.

He rejoined in P6 but made short work of cars ahead; in the final stages he closed the gap to George before making the pass for the lead with three laps left.

Our duo took the flag comfortably ahead of the rest of the field to secure the win, and the 50th for an Italian in F1.

Deputy Technical Director Simone Resta represented the team on the podium at his home race.

The team now leads the Constructors’ Championship by 122 points with Kimi heading the Drivers’ standings by 66 points from his team-mate George.

Profile

The Italian Grand Prix (Italian: Gran Premio d'Italia) is the fifth oldest national motor racing Grand Prix (after the French Grand Prix, the United States Grand Prix, the Spanish Grand Prix and the Russian Grand Prix), having been held since 1921. Since 2013, the Grand Prix has been held the most times, with 97 editions as of 2026.

It is one of the two Grands Prix (along with the British) which has run every season as an event of the Formula One World Championship Grands Prix, continuously since the championship was introduced in 1950.

Every Formula One Italian Grand Prix in the World Championship era has been held at Monza except in 1980, when it was held at Imola.

Profile

Mercedes-AMG Petronas Formula One Team

Mercedes-Benz, a German automotive brand of the Mercedes-Benz Group, has been involved in Formula One as both team owner and engine manufacturer for various periods since 1954. The current Mercedes-Benz Grand Prix Limited, competing as Mercedes-AMG Petronas Formula One Team, is based in Brackley, England, and holds a German racing licence. An announcement was made in December 2020 that Ineos planned to take a one third equal ownership stake alongside the Mercedes-Benz Group and Toto Wolff; this came into effect on 25 January 2022. Mercedes-branded teams are often referred to by the nickname, the "Silver Arrows" (German: Silberpfeile).

What makes the Austrian Grand Prix special – and why you should see it

Discover what makes the F1 weekend in Austria unmissable.

The Austrian Grand Prix is a classic, and might just be held at one of the most picturesque track on the F1 calendar. Set in the Styrian hills, around 700m above sea level, the short track features rapid lap times and plenty of overtaking opportunities.

Despite the Red Bull Ring having the fewest corners of any circuit on the schedule, it's seen many unforgettable moments throughout the years – and, as the name might suggest, is the track that Red Bull calls home.

Let's take a look at just some of the reasons why Austria is so alluring.

Austrian racing heritage

Austria, despite it's relatively small population, has heaps of racing heritage. Triple World Champion Niki Lauda was born in Vienna, winning titles for Ferrari and McLaren, and was a major factor behind Mercedes’ success while helping convince Lewis Hamilton to join the outfit in 2013.

Jochen Rindt was Austria's first champion – the only posthumous F1 title winner, having tragically passed away during his dominant 1970 season. Gerhard Berger, while never taking the title himself, scored 10 wins during his illustrious career.

More recently, the late Austrian entrepreneur Dietrich Mateschitz and former Austrian F1 racer Helmut Marko – in his role as motorsport advisor – played key roles in Red Bull's success, with the team clinching eight Drivers’ and six Constructors’ titles.

When is the 2026 Austrian Grand Prix?

The 2026 Austrian Grand Prix weekend begins on Friday 26 June, with F1 cars hitting the track for the first two Free Practice sessions, before Free Practice 3 and Qualifying take place on Saturday 27 June. The Grand Prix itself is on Sunday 28 June, at 1500 local time.

text:
BREAKING: “I DON’T GIVE A DAMN”! Trump BRAGS that America is making a "freaking fortune" from soaring oil prices while Americans suffer at the gas pump – and admits his own advisers warned him to keep his mouth shut about it!

Donald Trump just delivered an astonishing speech in which he openly acknowledged that Americans are hurting from high gas prices, boasted that American oil companies are making hundreds of billions of dollars, and then declared that he didn't care one iota about how it looked.

"We're making a freaking fortune!" Trump crowed at a rally in Georgia, after describing the enormous profits he claims American oil and gas companies are raking in because of the war in the Middle East.

The funny part is that Trump knew EXACTLY how his remarks would sound to struggling Americans.

"My people said, please don't mention that, sir, because people are paying a little higher," Trump told the crowd. But when it comes to the idea of anyone making money, Trump can't resist ...

"Our country is making hundreds of billions of dollars because of what's happened in the Middle East," he declared, naming Texas, Oklahoma, and Louisiana as places benefiting from the oil business.

He even claimed the windfall extended to Venezuela and Greenland, boasting that America was making "hundreds and hundreds of billions, trillions of dollars."

But who is this “America” person of whom he speaks -- the benfeciary of these trillions? America Ferrara, the actress? Captain America? Amerigo Vespucci? 

Trump imagined the headlines his remarks would generate, practically writing the criticism himself in a rare flash of self-awareness.

"President Trump is talking about all the money they're making while people are suffering at the pump," he said. "That'll be the headline."

But Trump never lets us down by not telling us how he really feels.
"But I said, I don't give a damn. I'm going to say it. We're making a freaking fortune."

Of course, there's a little distinction Trump seems determined to ignore: When oil companies make billions of dollars, that money doesn't magically appear in anyone’s bank account, unless you are an oil executive. The people suffering at the pump AREN’T sharing in any profits.

Trump again promised that oil prices would fall dramatically once the war ends, but offered no evidence of how or when that might happen.

Trump talks about the oil executives making billions as though their profits were his own personal triumph. He celebrates their windfall with unmistakable enthusiasm and even envy, even as he acknowledges that ordinary Americans are paying the bill for billions in profits.

He knows exactly how that sounds. He recited the criticism himself, practically word for word, before announcing that he didn't give a damn. And went right back to bragging about the money.

This is not the kind of president America wants or needs.
 
Vote Blue on November 3.

text:
Mediterranean diet may boost tiny proteins that protect the heart and brain | University of Southern California, ScienceDaily

A new study suggests that the Mediterranean diet may protect the heart, brain, and aging cells through a surprising biological mechanism involving tiny proteins produced by mitochondria, the structures responsible for generating most of the energy our cells need.

Researchers at the USC Leonard Davis School of Gerontology discovered that people who more closely followed the Mediterranean diet had higher levels of two mitochondrial microproteins called humanin and SHMOOSE. Both have previously been linked to protection against cardiovascular disease and neurodegeneration, the gradual deterioration of nerve cells that occurs in conditions such as Alzheimer's disease.

The study, led by USC Leonard Davis Instructional Associate Professor of Gerontology Roberto Vicinanza, offers a possible explanation for how everyday food choices influence cellular health and the aging process.

"These microproteins may act as molecular messengers that translate what we eat into how our cells function and age," Vicinanza said. "It's a new biological pathway that helps explain why the Mediterranean diet is so powerful."

How the Mediterranean Diet May Protect Aging Cells

The Mediterranean diet emphasizes foods such as olive oil, fish, beans, lentils, fruits, and vegetables. It has consistently been associated with a lower risk of heart disease, type 2 diabetes, and cognitive decline. However, scientists are still working to understand exactly how this eating pattern produces its wide-ranging health benefits.

To investigate, the researchers examined blood samples from older adults who followed the Mediterranean diet to different degrees. Those whose eating habits most closely matched the diet had significantly higher concentrations of humanin and SHMOOSE.

They also showed lower indicators of oxidative stress, a process in which harmful molecules called reactive oxygen species overwhelm the body's protective defenses. Over time, oxidative stress can damage proteins, DNA, and other cellular components, contributing to aging and chronic disease.

Interestingly, the researchers found that certain foods were associated with different microproteins. Higher consumption of olive oil, fish, and legumes was linked to increased humanin levels. Meanwhile, olive oil consumption and eating fewer refined carbohydrates were associated with higher levels of SHMOOSE.

Refined carbohydrates include foods made with heavily processed grains and sugars, such as white bread, pastries, and many sugary snacks. These foods generally contain less fiber and fewer naturally occurring nutrients than their minimally processed counterparts.

"These findings suggest that specific components of the Mediterranean diet may directly influence mitochondrial biology," said USC Leonard Davis School Dean and USC Distinguished Professor Pinchas Cohen, the study's senior author. "Humanin and SHMOOSE could serve as biomarkers for adherence to the Mediterranean diet and have clinical significance."

Biomarkers are measurable biological indicators that can provide information about a person's health or physiological state. In this case, the researchers suggest that humanin and SHMOOSE could eventually help scientists understand how closely someone's diet aligns with healthy eating patterns and how their cells respond.

Tiny Mitochondrial Proteins With Powerful Effects

The findings extend a scientific effort spanning more than 20 years to investigate small proteins produced by mitochondria. Cohen has played a leading role in discovering and studying these molecules, which are increasingly recognized as important participants in cellular health.

Mitochondria are often described as the powerhouses of cells because they produce much of the energy required for essential biological activities. But their role extends beyond energy production. They also help regulate metabolism, cellular stress responses, and processes associated with aging.

Unlike most proteins, which are produced using instructions stored in the DNA inside the cell's nucleus, mitochondrial microproteins originate from genetic instructions within mitochondria themselves.

These instructions are found in small segments of mitochondrial DNA known as open reading frames. Some of these regions were once considered nonfunctional, but researchers have discovered that they can encode biologically active molecules.

One of the best understood is humanin, first identified by Cohen and fellow researchers in 2003. Subsequent studies have associated humanin with improved insulin sensitivity, better cardiovascular health, increased longevity, and protection of cognitive abilities.

Insulin sensitivity refers to how effectively the body's cells respond to insulin, the hormone that helps regulate blood sugar. Maintaining healthy insulin sensitivity is important for metabolic health and reducing the risk of type 2 diabetes.

Another intriguing microprotein is SHMOOSE (Small Human Mitochondrial ORF Over SErine tRNA), which was identified more recently by Cohen's research team.

SHMOOSE has attracted particular interest because of its possible role in protecting the brain. Scientists have found that a genetic variant of SHMOOSE is associated with an increased risk of Alzheimer's disease. The normal version, meanwhile, appears to help protect neurons from damage involving amyloid, a protein that can accumulate abnormally in the brains of people with Alzheimer's.

"These peptides are emerging as key regulators of aging biology," Cohen said. "They connect mitochondrial function to diseases like Alzheimer's and heart disease and now, potentially, to nutrition."

A Hidden Mechanism for Protecting the Heart

The scientists also identified a potentially important connection between humanin and an enzyme called Nox2, which helps generate reactive oxygen species.

Although these molecules have useful roles in normal cell signaling and immune defense, excessive production can contribute to oxidative stress and damage blood vessels and other tissues.

The researchers observed that people with higher humanin levels tended to have lower Nox2 activity. This relationship raises the possibility that humanin helps limit damaging oxidative processes, potentially offering an additional layer of cardiovascular protection.

Based on these findings, the researchers propose that the Mediterranean diet could support heart health in two complementary ways. The diet may help reduce oxidative stress directly while also supporting the production of mitochondrial microproteins that influence pathways involved in cellular damage.

However, the observed associations do not establish that the diet directly increases these proteins or that the proteins themselves prevent cardiovascular disease.

"This could represent a new cardioprotective mechanism of the Mediterranean diet," Vicinanza said.

Bringing the Mediterranean Diet to a Global Audience

Vicinanza's interest in the Mediterranean diet extends beyond investigating its effects inside the body. He has also worked to promote this traditional eating pattern internationally as a way to support human health, cultural heritage, and environmental sustainability.

As part of those efforts, he collaborated with the Municipality of Pollica in Italy, which is recognized as a UNESCO Mediterranean Diet emblematic community.

That collaboration helped support the establishment of the International Day of the Mediterranean Diet through the United Nations.

Observed every year on November 16, the international event is intended to draw attention to the Mediterranean diet's health benefits as well as its cultural traditions and environmental significance.

For Vicinanza, the new findings reinforce the relationship between traditional food practices and modern discoveries about how the body functions.

"We're connecting centuries-old dietary traditions with cutting-edge molecular biology," Vicinanza said. "It supports the idea that healthy eating patterns with little to no ultra-processed foods reflect how humans have eaten over long periods and may create conditions to which mitochondria -- ancient cellular organelles -- are likely adapted."

Could Tiny Proteins Help Unlock Healthier Aging?

Although the findings are promising, the researchers emphasize that the study was relatively small and observational. That means it identified relationships between dietary habits and biological measurements but could not determine whether eating a Mediterranean diet directly caused the differences in microprotein levels.

Other factors, including participants' overall health and lifestyle, could also influence the results.

Nevertheless, the discovery opens an intriguing possibility for the emerging field of precision nutrition, which seeks to develop dietary recommendations based on an individual's biological characteristics and needs.

If future research confirms that dietary changes can reliably influence humanin, SHMOOSE, and related microproteins, these molecules could potentially become useful tools for evaluating nutritional interventions and developing more personalized strategies for healthy aging.

The next step is to determine whether adopting a Mediterranean-style diet actually increases these proteins and whether those changes lead to measurable improvements in cardiovascular health, brain function, or disease risk.

"Our goal is to move from observing associations to understanding causality," Vicinanza said. "If we can harness these pathways, we may be able to design nutritional strategies that promote healthy aging at the molecular level."
