text:
There is another lesson Nigerian political elites must learn. Not every contest must be fought immediately, and not every available opportunity must be seized simply because it exists.

Political impatience has damaged relationships, weakened parties and divided alliances that could otherwise have produced stronger outcomes. Politicians sometimes begin positioning themselves for offices they have not yet been formally offered, publicly challenge their political benefactors or interpret every disagreement as a signal to launch a new campaign for power.

The consequences can be costly.

The political careers of Bukola Saraki and Seyi Makinde, among others, demonstrate that political fortunes are shaped by changing alliances, party structures and disagreements over the distribution of power. Their experiences are different, and neither should be reduced to a simple story of ingratitude. Yet both illustrate the difficulty of balancing personal ambition with party loyalty and competing political interests.

The same caution applies to internal disagreements within the APC. Speculation about succession, the next presidential ticket and the future of influential officeholders can create unnecessary tension long before due time.

Where an incumbent has invested political capital in building a working relationship with an ally, any attempt to undermine that relationship should be weighed against the possible consequences. At the same time, no officeholder is entitled to automatic succession, and no political leader should be expected to surrender legitimate ambitions indefinitely.

The distinction is between ambition pursued with strategic patience and ambition pursued at the expense of every relationship that made political advancement possible.

Political maturity requires knowing when to compete, when to negotiate and when to wait.

Reciprocity is not political slavery

It is important to draw a line between repaying political favours and surrendering democratic judgement.

No president owns the votes of a region. No governor owns the votes of a state, and no political benefactor can legitimately demand permanent obedience from those he once supported. In a democracy, citizens retain the right to evaluate their leaders and choose their preferred candidates.

The argument for reciprocity should therefore be directed principally at political elites who have benefited from alliances and endorsements, not used to silence citizens who have legitimate grievances about economic hardship, insecurity, unemployment or public services.

President Tinubu’s re-election prospects will ultimately depend on more than the goodwill of political leaders. His administration must convince Nigerians that its policies are improving their lives and that the sacrifices associated with its economic reforms will produce tangible and broad-based benefits.

The opposition, in turn, has every right to challenge the administration and present an alternative programme. Political competition is not ingratitude, just as political loyalty is not proof of good governance.

The strongest argument for Tinubu’s second term is one that combines the history of political alliances with a convincing account of what his administration has achieved, what remains unfinished and what Nigerians can reasonably expect over another four years.

Reciprocity may strengthen a political coalition, but performance must sustain it.

The burden of political memory

The Kaduna rally has placed a question before northern political elites: will they treat their relationship with Tinubu as a temporary arrangement or as a long-term political partnership?

For those who believe the President deserves another term because of his past support for northern leaders, the next step is to demonstrate that commitment through organised, lawful and sustained political engagement. Statements of solidarity are a beginning, not the conclusion of the process.

text:
🌿THE BEAUTIFUL BRAIN🌿
PART 9 | CREATIVITY IS AN ANTIDOTE TO RUMINATION

The Science of Wonder | A MindConfetti Series

✨WHEN THE MIND GETS STUCK

Have you ever noticed how the mind can become trapped in an endless conversation with itself? A difficult encounter is replayed repeatedly. An unanswered question produces countless hypothetical explanations. Yesterday's frustrations become tomorrow's anticipated problems. 

👉🏻Psychologists call this process rumination: repetitive thinking focused on distress, its causes and its consequences, often without producing meaningful solutions. While reflection can help us understand experiences, rumination frequently keeps us circling the same emotional territory. Research associates persistent rumination with increased vulnerability to anxiety and depression. The remarkable thing is that sometimes the way out of repetitive thinking does not begin with another thought. It begins with doing something different.

✨THE NEUROSCIENCE OF MENTAL LOOPS

The brain contains interacting networks involved in internally directed thought, attention and cognitive control. The default mode network, for example, participates in autobiographical memory, self-referential thinking and imagining possible futures. Although this network is sometimes associated with rumination, it also supports valuable functions, including creativity and reflection. Rumination cannot be reduced to one brain region or network. Rather, it involves patterns of thinking and emotional processing that become difficult to disengage from. Activities requiring sustained, meaningful attention may help interrupt these patterns by redirecting cognitive resources toward the present.

✨WHY CREATIVITY CAN INTERRUPT RUMINATION

Painting, gardening, photography, dancing, playing music and writing all invite the mind into active engagement. They involve sensory information, movement, imagination and decision-making. Instead of endlessly reviewing what happened yesterday, attention becomes occupied with selecting colors, arranging shapes, following rhythms or discovering possibilities. Research suggests that certain creative activities can reduce stress and support emotional regulation, although evidence for their specific effects on rumination remains developing. Creativity is not a guaranteed cure for repetitive thinking, but it can offer a constructive alternative to remaining mentally immobilized.

✨THE POWER OF FLOW

Psychologist Mihaly Csikszentmihalyi popularized the concept of flow, a state of deep absorption in an activity that offers an appropriate balance between challenge and skill. During flow, attention becomes concentrated, self-consciousness may diminish and the passage of time can feel different. 

👉🏻Creative pursuits can provide opportunities for this experience. Interestingly, flow is not necessarily about relaxation. It often involves active concentration and meaningful effort. The mind becomes occupied with something sufficiently engaging that repetitive self-focused thoughts may temporarily lose their dominance.

📊 𝗗𝗲𝗲𝗽 𝗗𝗶𝘃𝗲: 𝗔𝗽𝗼𝗹𝗹𝗼 𝗠𝗶𝗰𝗿𝗼 𝗦𝘆𝘀𝘁𝗲𝗺𝘀 𝗤𝟮 𝗙𝗬𝟮𝟳 𝗘𝗮𝗿𝗻𝗶𝗻𝗴𝘀 𝗖𝗮𝗹𝗹🚀

🏢 Company Overview: What Does Apollo Micro Systems Do?

Apollo Micro Systems (AMS) designs and makes mission-critical defense electronics, sensors, RF and control systems, and pyrotechnics for naval, air, missile defense, and space platforms. 🛡️

🧩 Evolution: Moving from a Tier 2/3 subsystem supplier to an integrated player building complete weapon systems and long-range platforms. ⚙️

💥 Ideal Explosives: Subsidiary in commercial explosives and defense energetics. It commissioned an 8.5-acre, 9,000 MT bulk storage silo near Asansol for Coal India orders. 🏭

🤝 Premier Explosives: CCI approval received and the open offer is underway. 📑

🚀 Shauryastra Defense Systems: New associate company led by Dr. V.K. Saraswat (ex-DRDO Chairman) to design complete indigenous long-range (300+ km) weapon platforms. 🎯

🔬 Technology: Awarded MoD Transfer of Technology (ToT) for the Semi-Active Laser Homing System. 🏅

🌐 Industry Structure

Policy Tailwinds: Make in India, military modernization, and indigenization are driving a structural growth phase. 📈

Entry Barriers: New entrants need 4–5 years to clear qualification standards, audits, and technology absorption. 🔒

Sole-Source Status: AMS holds proprietary or sole-supplier status on key subsystems, including electronic passive systems, navigation, and onboard computers for MIGM and QRSAM. 👑

Order Splitting: MoD is splitting major production runs between PSUs and private industry (QRSAM missiles 50/50, multi-vendor for Pinaka). 🤝

📈 Financial Performance

Q2 FY27 Consolidated:

Revenue: ₹388 Crores (+72% YoY, +54% QoQ). 🚀

EBITDA: ₹111 Crores (+88% YoY, +107% QoQ). Margin 29% (+200 bps YoY). 💰

PAT: ₹46 Crores (+40% YoY, +83% QoQ). 🎯

Q2 FY27 Standalone:

Revenue: ₹306 Crores (+36% YoY, +96% QoQ). 📊

EBITDA: ₹108 Crores (+82% YoY). Margin 35% (+900 bps YoY). ⚡

PAT: ₹48 Crores (+46% YoY). 💵

H1 FY27 Consolidated:

Revenue: ₹639 Crores (+78% YoY, vs ₹359 Cr in H1 FY26). 📈

EBITDA: ₹165 Crores (+65% YoY). 💰

PAT: ₹71 Crores (+50% YoY). 🎯

Operating Cash Flow: Positive at ₹22 Crores. 🏦

Working Capital: 353 days (vs 359 days in FY26). 🔄

H1 FY27 Standalone:

Revenue: ₹462 Crores (+29% YoY). 🚀

EBITDA: ₹156 Crores (+56% YoY), with an all-time-high margin of 34% (+600 bps YoY). ⚡

PAT: ₹76 Crores (+44% YoY), with margin up to 16% (+200 bps YoY). 💵

Order Book: All-time high ₹1,765 Crores as of September 30, 2026 (~₹1,300 Cr Standalone and ~₹465 Cr Ideal Explosives). 📦

Tax: Q2 standalone effective tax rate was ~51% after moving to the old regime (30% slab) on crossing the ₹400 Cr turnover threshold. 🧾

🔮 Growth Guidance

FY27 Revenue: Growth guidance of 35–45% maintained. 🚀

Order Book: Base order book to reach ₹2,000+ Crores by March 2027, excluding MIGM. Including the anticipated MIGM order, total holdings could scale to ₹4,500–5,000 Crores. 📈

5-Year Aspiration: ₹25,000 Crore group revenue, driven by energetics, integrated platforms, and acquisitions. 🏆

💰 Margin Guidance

EBITDA Outlook: Standalone margin of 34–35% reflects a higher mix of production orders over R&D projects. Margins will fluctuate quarter to quarter with mix. 📊

Cash Conversion: Structural improvement in operating cash flow relative to PAT is expected from FY29 onwards, as high-volume production orders with advance payments replace development projects. 🔄

🏭 Strategic Customer Pipeline & Volume Visibility

MIGM (Mines & Torpedo Countermeasure): Naval HQ RFQ expected in November 2026, with PO targeted for Jan–Mar 2027. It carries a 20% advance, user trials are complete, and AMS is the sole source for electronic passive systems and sensors. ⚓

Pinaka Rockets: RFQ submitted for the 300-unit MIL case, with order finalization expected before December 2026. Visibility covers 4,000 rockets (2,000 Army + 2,000 Armenia exports). 🚀

QRSAM: Initial 1,000-missile order split 50% BDL and 50% private. AMS supplies navigation and onboard computers, while Premier provides propulsion. 🎯

Heavyweight Torpedoes: Emergency RFP to BDL for 30 units (9-month execution), expected in November 2026, followed by a larger 125-unit order. 🌊

Varanasi & Others: ₹100+ Cr of inflows expected from Varanasi, plus participation in Pralay, MoD-MAN, Limpet Mines, and RGP-60 rockets. 💥

📊 𝗖𝗮𝗽𝗮𝗰𝗶𝘁𝘆 𝗨𝘁𝗶𝗹𝗶𝘇𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻 & 𝗘𝘅𝗽𝗮𝗻𝘀𝗶𝗼𝗻

Unit 3: Phase 1 is operational. Full completion expands capacity to 12x the original facility, creating headroom for foreign export orders from FY28. 🏗️

In-House Testing: Dedicated EMI/EMC test facilities and navigation calibration rigs (operational within a month) remove dependence on third-party DRDO labs and cut production cycle times. 🔬

Energetics: 9,000 MT silo across 8.5 acres in Asansol will serve Coal India subsidiaries and defense energetics logistics. 💥

🔍 Noticeable Trends

Complete Systems: Moving up from Tier 2 components to turnkey weapon platforms, missile systems, and energetics integration. 🚀

Private Sector Push: Up to 50% of major missile and platform orders are being allocated to private industry. 🤝

Exports: International defense exports are planned once Unit 3 reaches full scale, targeting global supply chains (e.g., EU REAM Europe). 🌍

ToT Awards: Direct MoD/DRDO technology transfers to qualified private firms are accelerating indigenous readiness. 🏅

⚠️ Risk

Subsidiary Turnaround: Ideal Explosives is in a 4-quarter transition to fix thin margins and seasonal lean quarters. 🏭

Order Lumpiness: MoD procurement timing shifts can cause quarter-to-quarter swings in revenue and order book. 📅

Working Capital: High at 353 days due to inventory and development-stage payment cycles until FY29. 🔄

Integration: Scaling electronics, Ideal Explosives, and the upcoming Premier acquisition in parallel needs seamless leadership and monitoring. 🧩

🎙️ Management Tone

Confident & Upbeat: Positive on record top line, EBITDA, and PAT, execution, and order visibility. 🗣️

Long-Term Focus: Stresses building technology "brick by brick" and positioning the group as an indigenous global OEM over the next 5–6 years. 🏛️

Transparent & Disciplined: Withholding joint guidance on Premier Explosives until the acquisition completes, while staying transparent on project timelines. 🎯

𝗪𝗵𝗮𝘁 𝗟𝗼𝗻𝗴-𝗧𝗲𝗿𝗺 𝗜𝗻𝘃𝗲𝘀𝘁𝗼𝗿𝘀 𝗦𝗵𝗼𝘂𝗹𝗱 𝗧𝗿𝗮𝗰𝗸 🚀

Going through the Q2 FY27 call again with a 2-year lens (FY27 to FY28), these are the points I would keep on my radar. 👇

💵 𝗖𝗮𝘀𝗵 𝗙𝗹𝗼𝘄 & 𝗪𝗼𝗿𝗸𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗖𝗮𝗽𝗶𝘁𝗮𝗹: 𝗧𝗵𝗲 𝗙𝗬𝟮𝟵 𝗟𝗮𝗴

Working Capital: Still heavy at 353 days in H1 FY27 (359 days in FY26). 🔄

Cash Conversion: Management is clear that consistent, strong operating cash flow comes only from FY29 onwards. So over a 2-year hold, profit growth will likely outpace cash growth. 📊

Why the Lag: The mix still has a lot of early-stage R&D and development projects. From FY29, large production orders with advance payments (MIGM carries 20%) should anchor cash conversion. 🏦

📦 𝗖𝗮𝘁𝗮𝗹𝘆𝘀𝘁 𝗧𝗶𝗺𝗲𝗹𝗶𝗻𝗲 & 𝗢𝗿𝗱𝗲𝗿 𝗕𝗼𝗼𝗸

Current Order Book: ₹1,765 Cr as of Sept 30, 2026 (~₹1,300 Cr Standalone, ~₹465 Cr Ideal Explosives). 📈

Base Order Book: Expected at ₹2,000+ Cr by March 2027, excluding MIGM. 🎯

MIGM (the big one): Naval HQ RFQ in November 2026, PO targeted for Jan–Mar 2027 with a 20% advance. Including MIGM, total holdings could reach ₹4,500–5,000 Cr, with an execution window of ~18 months. ⚓

Pinaka Rockets: 300-unit MIL case RFQ submitted, order expected before December 2026. Visibility of 4,000 rockets (2,000 domestic Army + 2,000 Armenia exports). 🚀

Heavyweight Torpedoes: Emergency RFP to BDL for 30 units on a 9-month schedule (expected November 2026), followed by a larger 125-unit order. 🌊

🧾 𝗧𝗮𝘅 𝗗𝗶𝘀𝗰𝗼𝗻𝘁𝗶𝗻𝘂𝗶𝘁𝘆 & 𝗡𝗲𝘁 𝗠𝗮𝗿𝗴𝗶𝗻

Tax Jump: Q2 standalone effective tax rate spiked to ~51%. 📉

Reason: Crossing the ₹400 Cr turnover threshold moved the company from the 25% slab to the 30% base rate under the old regime. 🔁

What It Means: EBITDA margin hit a record 35% in Q2 standalone, but PAT growth will lag operating growth for a while because of this tax friction. ⚡

🏗️ 𝗨𝗻𝗶𝘁 𝟯 𝗦𝗰𝗮𝗹𝗶𝗻𝗴 & 𝗕𝗼𝘁𝘁𝗹𝗲𝗻𝗲𝗰𝗸 𝗥𝗲𝗺𝗼𝘃𝗮𝗹

In-House Testing: EMI/EMC test facilities and navigation calibration rigs go live within a month. 🔬

Cycle Time: This cuts dependence on third-party DRDO labs, where delays used to run into weeks or months, and should speed up revenue recognition. ⏱️

Capacity: Unit 3 Phase 1 is operational. Full completion takes capacity to 12x the original size and opens up foreign defense exports from FY28. 🌍

⚠️ 𝗠&𝗔 𝗘𝘅𝗲𝗰𝘂𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻 & 𝗦𝘂𝗯𝘀𝗶𝗱𝗶𝗮𝗿𝘆 𝗗𝗿𝗮𝗴

Ideal Explosives: H1 consolidated PAT (₹71 Cr) is below standalone PAT (₹76 Cr) because of thin commercial explosives margins and a lean off-season. Turnaround is expected to take 2–4 quarters. 🏭

Premier Explosives: CCI approval cleared the open offer. Joint guidance is on hold until the deal closes (~1 month), followed by a joint investor call. 🤝

Shauryastra Defense Systems: New associate led by Dr. V.K. Saraswat (ex-DRDO Chairman) to design complete 300+ km weapon platforms, moving AMS from subsystem vendor toward platform OEM. 🎯

🎯 𝗠𝘆 𝗧𝗮𝗸𝗲

Over 24 months, the story is order inflow (MIGM, Pinaka, torpedoes) and execution, not cash generation. Cash conversion is an FY29 story, so I would track the MIGM PO timing and the working capital days each quarter. 🔍

Do you think MIGM lands by March 2027? 👇

📊 𝗔𝗽𝗼𝗹𝗹𝗼 𝗠𝗶𝗰𝗿𝗼 𝗦𝘆𝘀𝘁𝗲𝗺𝘀 𝗤𝟮 𝗙𝗬𝟮𝟳 𝗖𝗼𝗻𝗰𝗮𝗹𝗹: 𝗞𝗲𝘆 𝗤&𝗔 🚀

⚓ Q1. What is the status of the MIGM order, when is the RFQ expected, and will user trials delay execution? (Asked by Dikshan, DB Wealth)

💬 A. (Karunakar Reddy Baddam, MD) Naval HQ RFQ is expected in November 2026. The Navy plans to issue the final purchase order between January and February 2027, and not later than March. The sanction carries a 20% advance payment to be released before the financial year-end. User trials are 100% complete, so no further trials are needed before series production. Apollo is the sole source for the electronic passive systems and critical sensors, with no second source set up by DRDO. 🎯

📈 Q2. Standalone revenue grew ~30% in H1. Will H2 close the gap to annual guidance? (Asked by Amit Kumar, HDFC Securities & Angush Agrawal, Surge Capital)

💬 A. (Krishna Sai Kumar Addepalli, ED & Karunakar Reddy Baddam, MD) FY27 top-line growth guidance of 35–45% is maintained. The ₹1,765 Cr order book (~₹1,300 Cr Standalone, ~₹465 Cr Ideal Explosives) should reach ₹2,000+ Cr by March 2027 excluding MIGM. Once MIGM is awarded, total holdings scale to ₹4,500–5,000 Cr. 📦

💵 Q3. What is the target for operating cash flow, and when will cash conversion match reported PAT? (Asked by Gaurav Shukla, Finwizz)

💬 A. (Krishna Sai Kumar Addepalli, ED) Consistent, positive operating cash flow across all quarters will materialize from FY29 onwards. Today's revenue still carries a higher share of development and R&D projects. From FY29, large production orders with advance payments and regular milestone execution will anchor the model and align profit with cash. 🔄

🏭 Q4. Consolidated PAT (₹71 Cr) is below Standalone PAT (₹76 Cr) because of Ideal Explosives. What is the turnaround plan, and when does Premier close? (Asked by Amit Dixit, Goldman Sachs & Ronak Sanghvi, NAFA Capital)

💬 A. (Krishna Sai Kumar Addepalli, ED & Karunakar Reddy Baddam, MD) Ideal was a loss-making acquisition with thin commercial margins. Management is restructuring costs and expanding logistics for defense energetics, with improvement expected in 2–4 quarters. Q2 was also an off-season lean quarter for commercial explosives. Ideal has commissioned an 8.5-acre, 9,000 MT bulk storage silo in Asansol for Coal India orders. CCI approval has cleared the Premier open offer. Joint guidance is on hold until the deal completes (~1 month), after which a joint investor call will be held. 🤝

🧾 Q5. Why did the Standalone Q2 effective tax rate jump to ~51%? (Asked by Ronak Sanghvi, NAFA Capital)

💬 A. (Krishna Sai Kumar Addepalli, ED) Crossing the ₹400 Cr turnover threshold in the prior reference years moved the company from the 25% slab to the 30% base rate under the old tax regime, which drove higher tax provisions in the quarter. 📉

🛡️ Q6. What is driving MoD procurement timing, and how does order-splitting affect Apollo? (Asked by Penakin, HSBC & Abhijit Singh, Systematics)

💬 A. (Karunakar Reddy Baddam, MD) MoD is splitting major platform orders between PSUs and private firms, for example the 1,000-missile QRSAM order at 50% BDL and 50% private. Apollo is the sole established supplier for navigation and onboard computers, while Premier provides propulsion. For Pinaka, the 300-unit MIL case RFQ is submitted, with orders expected before December 2026 and a pipeline of 4,000 rockets (2,000 domestic Army + 2,000 Armenia exports). The Navy has issued an emergency RFP to BDL for 30 heavyweight torpedoes (9-month delivery, targeted November 2026), followed by a larger 125-unit order. 🚀

🏗️ Q7. How will the Unit 3 expansion affect export potential and manufacturing lead times? (Asked by Penakin, HSBC & Jimeet Jain, Wealth Mine Advisory)

💬 A. (Karunakar Reddy Baddam, MD & Krishna Sai Kumar Addepalli, ED) Unit 3 Phase 1 is operational. Once fully complete, capacity expands to 12x the original size, enabling international export pursuits from FY28. Apollo is also installing in-house EMI/EMC test facilities and navigation calibration rigs (operational within a month), removing dependence on third-party DRDO labs where testing delays used to run into weeks or months. 🔬

🎯 Q8. What is the objective and structure of the new associate entity, Shauryastra Defense Systems? (Asked by Abhishek Kamdar, Value Plus Advisors)

💬 A. (Karunakar Reddy Baddam, MD) It is led by Dr. V.K. Saraswat (former Scientific Advisor to Raksha Mantri, ex-DRDO Chairman, NITI Aayog member). The aim is to fill national technology gaps by designing complete indigenous long-range weapon platforms (300+ km, versus the current 120 km Pinaka limit), moving Apollo from a Tier 2/3 subsystem supplier to a primary weapon platform OEM. 💥

🏆 Q9. What supports the ₹25,000 Cr group revenue target in 5 years, and what are the entry barriers for competitors? (Asked by Kaushik, BPCL)

💬 A. text:
Yeah, like trust Putin, only a retard will accept.

"Putin offered peace and Ukraine said no." Let's look at what he actually offered.
Istanbul, 2022. The one everyone cites. Ukraine put neutrality on the table. Russia's April draft in return: cap Ukraine's army at a fraction of its size, give Moscow a veto over the security guarantees meant to protect Ukraine from Moscow, and keep every inch Russia had grabbed. That's not a peace deal. That's a disarmament order with a signature line. Ukraine walked away in May — after Bucha, and after Russia's terms got harder, not softer.

June 2024. The night before a peace summit he wasn't invited to, Putin announced a "real peace proposal": Ukraine withdraws from four entire regions including land Russia doesn't control, renounces NATO forever, demilitarizes, and sanctions get lifted. Then Russia stops shooting. If your neighbor demands your house and your car before he'll stop punching you, you haven't been offered a deal. You've been offered terms of surrender.

2025. Europe and the US proposed an unconditional 30-day ceasefire. Ukraine accepted on the spot. Putin's answer: talks "without preconditions" — on the precondition they're based on the 2022 draft and "the situation on the battlefield." Both sides swapped memos. Putin's own words: "absolutely contradictory." Prisoners got exchanged. The shooting didn't stop.

2026. Trump's team floats a compromise. Ukraine answers with a 20-point counter. Russia kills it over the one clause that would have made it stick: European troops guaranteeing the ceasefire. As of June, Putin's position is unchanged — Istanbul 2022 or nothing.

Four years. Four "offers." One set of terms: give up territory you still hold, give up your allies, shrink your army, trust us.

text:
Audi plans $4 billion Georgia plant with capacity for up to 200,000 vehicles a year

Audi has defended a planned $4 billion investment in a Georgia factory, presenting it as a way to grow U.S. sales and limit the effect of tariffs on its business. The facility would be the company’s first plant in the United States, and its planned annual capacity reaches up to 200,000 vehicles. Audi expects roughly half of that output to go to markets outside the country, so the plant is not described as serving U.S. buyers alone. The Guardian also characterized the project as a $4bn (£3bn) investment and a first U.S. factory, while reporting that the intended output is 200,000 SUVs.

The path to selecting Georgia followed months of work: Audi assessed more than 70 potential U.S. sites and held discussions with public officials. The company plans to start building the Q7, Q8 and Q9 at the site in the early 2030s. A U.S. official told Reuters that those same three SUV lines were expected to be assembled there. The Guardian reported that the production plan would move some manufacturing from Bratislava, Slovakia, while Audi’s stated export share indicates that the Georgia output is intended to reach customers beyond the United States.

Audi says its U.S. ambitions exceed its current reach: Chief Executive Gernot Dollner said the company is not capturing the full opportunity in the American premium-car market. Audi of America President Vito Paladino described the goal as becoming a consequential competitor in the United States and said further information about investment and production would come later. The plant is also expected to support about 4,500 jobs, according to Audi’s announcement as reported by cnBeta. The Guardian likewise reported a 4,500-job figure, describing those positions alongside production of 200,000 SUVs.

The available sales figures describe a difficult U.S. backdrop, though they refer to different periods: deliveries were roughly unchanged through the third quarter after a 16% decline from 2024 to 2025. A separate cnBeta account said Audi sales had fallen for two years, reporting a 7% decrease in the first half of 2026 and a 16% drop in U.S. sales that year. Those accounts do not present one interchangeable measure: one gives U.S. deliveries through the third quarter and compares 2024 with 2025, while the other specifies first-half sales and a U.S. annual decline. The company’s case for expansion therefore sits alongside reported weakness in sales, as well as its stated view that the U.S. premium-car market still offers room to grow.

Tariffs are another stated reason for producing in the United States: Audi imports every vehicle it sells there from Europe or Mexico. Those duties cost Audi 1.2 billion euros ($1.4 billion) last year, according to CNBC’s account. The U.S. charge on vehicles from Germany stood at 15%, lower than its previous 25% level. Volkswagen, Audi’s parent, said tariffs cost it as much as €5bn(£4.2bn)a year before reduced sales were included, a broader company figure that should not be confused with Audi’s own reported cost. Volkswagen chief Oliver Blume told investors in July that U.S. tariffs were a substantial strain and limited trade across borders.

Dollner said the U.S. administration had asked Audi to announce the project at a Georgia rally before the Nov. 3 midterm elections. He also characterized the plant as the result of a three-year process, saying its timing matched the rally rather than originating with it. The Guardian reported that Dollner joined Trump onstage at a campaign event in Macon, Georgia, for the factory announcement. Audi’s explanation thus links the timing of the public announcement to the event while describing the underlying project as having begun earlier.

Dollner said Georgia production would not remove work from Germany, which he described as central to Audi’s operations. That assurance comes as Volkswagen plans to eliminate 50,000 jobs and shut four German plants, including an Audi site, between 2031 and 2034. The Guardian separately reported that Volkswagen had started cutting as many as 100,000 jobs and closing German factories, citing Chinese competition, tariffs and the cost of investment in the transition to electric vehicles for markets beyond the United States. The two job accounts use different descriptions and scales, so the 50,000 planned reductions and the report of as many as 100,000 cuts should not be treated as the same count.

The Georgia project is not the only production plan described in the reporting: an unnamed U.S. official said Audi also intended to make 2.5万辆 vehicles each year in neighboring South Carolina. That official also said Volkswagen would assemble vehicles at a Scout Motors plant being built in Blythewood, near Columbia, South Carolina. Dollner framed the Georgia choice around Audi’s confidence in the American market and its decision to bring its largest, highest-end SUVs there. Taken together, the reporting supports a picture of U.S. expansion taking place alongside German job cuts and factory closures, rather than a change consisting only of moving production from one country to another.

The sources also describe a possible China-based production route, but present it as an unapproved proposal rather than a settled Audi decision. The reported idea was to build a next-generation A8 for China with Huawei technology in China, instead of sending that model from Germany. The report said production could begin by the end of 2028 and would restore activity at Audi’s Changchun PPE factory. It forecast Audi’s 2026 worldwide sales at only slightly above 140万辆 and its China sales at only above 42万辆, roughly 30% below 2025. IT之家 also reported that Zhang Jun would take over as Audi’s China president on 2026 年 11 月 1 日, becoming the first Chinese national to hold the post. Together, the U.S. plans and the reported China proposal support a description of production strategies developing in both countries, not a single transfer of Audi’s manufacturing base.

text:
Zuccaro Rules, Punters Lose Their Bearings

Heavy overnight rain threatened to wash out the Invitation Cup weekend at Mysore, but the weather gods relented, only for the favourites to face a storm of their own. With long shots ruling the roost and punters left counting their losses, Zuccaro’s commanding triumph in the Zavaray Poonawalla Indian Turf Invitation Cup provided a reassuring display of class amid the chaos. The Mysore Race Club delivered, but the betting ring witnessed a different story.

By Sharan Kumar

The Invitation Cup was a coronation, the Super Mile a surprise, and the weekend a punters’ nightmare as long shots repeatedly stole the limelight at Mysore.

Heavy overnight rain threatened to play spoilsport, but the Mysore Race Club was fortunate to have the weather gods on its side on Sunday. The rain stayed away during racing, though the favourites appeared to have received no such assurance. One by one, the fancied runners were swept aside, leaving punters nursing their wounds and wondering whether the form book had been left out in the rain. With a majority of the 18 races over the weekend going to horses quoted at odds of 10 to 1 or more, the Invitation Cup weekend turned into a festival of surprises, with the betting ring providing more drama than the racecourse itself.

The Zavaray Poonawalla Indian Turf Invitation Cup, the star attraction of Sunday's Mysore races, was the one contest in which the result offered little suspense. The six-year-old Zuccaro from Pesi Shroff's stable towered over a patched-up opposition, and the race had virtually ceased to be a contest once the final line-up was announced.

There was a time when the Invitation Cup was a fiercely competitive championship, bringing together the best horses from across the country. In recent years, however, the race has lost some of its old aura. The Indian Derby winner, who ought to be a natural contender for the country's premier weight-for-age contest, is often missing, frequently because of niggles picked up during a demanding campaign. If memory serves right, Desert God was the last Indian Derby winner to complete the double.

The four-kilogram advantage once enjoyed by four-year-olds has also been done away with, leaving the Grade 1 race without penalties. The change has arguably tilted the balance towards older horses, and proven campaigners such as Adjudicate and Juliet have enjoyed repeated success in the event. The Invitation Cup, which once promised a clash between the country's emerging champions and established stars, has increasingly become a showcase for the old guard.

This year, Zuccaro ensured there would be no argument about the outcome. The six-year-old, who had clocked an astonishing time in the Maharaja's Cup at Bangalore, was in a different league from his rivals. Moving with raking strides on turning for home, he overhauled the leaders on the bridle before stretching away to win by a distance. Jockey Vivek G hardly had to move a muscle, making the finish look more like a leisurely exercise than a battle for one of Indian racing's most coveted prizes.

Zuccaro, a son of Kingda Ka, has been a sensational performer, and Sunday's victory was another emphatic demonstration of his class. Provided he remains physically sound, there should be more big-race honours in store.

Redefined, the previous year's Invitation Cup winner, has endured a succession of niggles and could manage only a narrow second, necking out the pace-setting Duke of Tuscany. The effort was hardly reassuring, as Redefined returned lame after the race. For Zuccaro, it was a coronation; for the opposition, it was an uncomfortable reminder of the gulf in class.

Echoes of Time Makes Punters Pay

If the Invitation Cup was a foregone conclusion, the Grade 1 Maj P K Mehra Memorial Super Mile Cup provided a very different spectacle. Aravind Ganapathy-trained Echoes of Time, who had stumbled the previous day in the Sprinters Cup and failed to make an impression, bounced back with a vengeance to deny Pride's Prince in the closing strides.

Shamrock, the winner of the previous year's race, was the favourite, with Alfonsine, the champion horse of the Bangalore Summer Season, also attracting substantial support. The race suffered an early setback when Alfonsine was withdrawn at the gates on veterinary grounds.

That did little to improve Shamrock's prospects. The heavy underfoot conditions appeared to take their toll, and the fancied runner struggled to finish a distant third.

Imtiaz Sait-trained Pride's Prince, meanwhile, took the race by the scruff of its neck, leading aggressively and fighting for every inch of the journey. He looked capable of carrying his challenge all the way, only for Echoes of Time, ridden with determination by Aashad Asbar, to produce a late burst and snatch victory by a neck.

It was a memorable triumph for former trainer Ganapathy, who had won this prestigious race on several occasions during his training career. This time, however, he celebrated from a different vantage point, as the owner of the winner. Watching his son achieve success in a race that had brought him so much distinction must have made the occasion particularly special.
The Super Mile also captured the mood of the weekend. Two long shots dominated the finish while the horses backed by the punters failed to deliver. The form book was not merely upset; it was given a thorough shaking.

Frederika Defies the Ratings

Jockey Akshay Kumar had a weekend to remember, and his victory aboard Frederika in the Grade 2 Suresh Mahindra Multi Million added another highlight to his impressive tally.

Frederika was required to fend off the well-backed Money Bags, who disappointed his supporters for the second consecutive day after an underwhelming performance in the Sprinters Cup.

Akshay Kumar sent Frederika into the lead and dictated the pace. Money Bags appeared to have the leader in trouble when mounting a strong challenge, but Frederika found more reserves of energy than his rating suggested and fought back gamely to prevail by just under a length.

Money Bags veered out under pressure, losing some of his momentum at a crucial stage. African Gold finished third, while Hyderabad's favourite Gachchhatu struggled to handle the prevailing conditions and finished fourth.

The ratings made the outcome all the more interesting. Money Bags and African Gold were rated considerably higher than Frederika, whose rating stood at 58. Yet it was Frederika who ran well above his mark, while the more fancied runners failed to justify their standing. His rating will rise substantially by after this performance.

Frederika is by Fiero, the Manjri Stud Farm stallion who also sired Ranquelino, last year's Indian Derby winner.

The victory was another feather in the cap of S John, who recently secured his licence as a racehorse trainer after a successful career as a jockey. Training for his patron P Arun Kumar, John enjoyed a memorable weekend, saddling winners of the Grade 1 Sprinters Cup and the Grade 2 Suresh Mahindra Multi Million. The stable's colours were prominent among the local brigade, making it a particularly rewarding weekend for the newly licensed trainer.

The Weather Behaved, the Form Did Not
There had been genuine apprehension about Sunday's racing after a heavy downpour overnight. The Mysore track is capable of absorbing considerable rainfall and remaining raceable, provided the showers do not continue through the day. Fortunately, the weather cooperated, allowing the Invitation Cup programme to proceed with the pomp and ceremony befitting the occasion.

The form book, however, was another matter. With long shots repeatedly finding their way into the winner's enclosure, punters who relied on established form had a thoroughly uncomfortable weekend. The favourites were conspicuous more for their failures than their victories, while horses at double-digit odds repeatedly gate-crashed the celebrations.

The Mysore Race Club deserves credit for ensuring that the weekend went ahead despite the threat posed by the weather and for conducting the meeting with the pomp and grandeur befitting the occasion. The Invitation Cup retained its ceremonial splendour, and Zuccaro supplied a champion worthy of the occasion. However, the Mysore Race Club, along with other racing clubs across the country, owes a special word of gratitude to Zavaray Poonawalla for his generous sponsorship and, more importantly, his unflagging enthusiasm and determination to do everything possible to keep Indian racing alive and kicking. At a time when the sport needs committed patrons more than ever, his continued support is a welcome reminder that racing still has champions beyond the racecourse.

For the punters, though, the weekend offered a rather different takeaway. The rain stayed away, the races went off without a hitch, and the champions had their moment. It was only the betting slips that ended up thoroughly soaked.
